units.text: Love righteousness, you who judge the earth; think of the Lord in goodness, and seek Him in simplicity of heart.
For He is found by those who do not put Him to the test, and He makes Himself known to those who do not distrust Him.
For crooked reasonings separate from God, and power, when put to the test, exposes the foolish.
For wisdom will not enter a soul that devises evil, nor will she dwell in a body indebted to sin.
For a holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit and depart from senseless reasonings, and will be put to shame when injustice comes upon it.

For wisdom is a spirit that loves humanity, and she will not acquit a blasphemer of what his lips have said; for God is a witness of his kidneys, a true overseer of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.
For the Spirit of the Lord has filled the inhabited world, and that which holds all things together has knowledge of utterance.
Therefore no one who speaks unjust things will escape notice, nor will convicting justice pass him by.
For there will be an examination of the ungodly person’s deliberations, and the report of his words will come to the Lord to expose his lawless deeds.
For an ear of jealousy listens to all things, and the murmur of grumblings is not hidden.
Therefore guard yourselves against useless grumbling, and restrain your tongue from slander; for a secret utterance will not pass away without effect, and a lying mouth destroys a soul.
Do not pursue death through the wandering of your life, nor draw destruction upon yourselves through the works of your hands;
For God did not make death, neither does He delight in the destruction of the living.
For He created all things that they might exist, and the created things of the world are life-preserving; there is no poison of destruction in them, nor is Hades’ dominion upon the earth.
For righteousness is immortal.
But the ungodly summoned him by their hands and words; considering him a friend, they wasted away, and they made a covenant with him, because they are worthy to belong to his portion.
For they said among themselves, reasoning wrongly: “Our life is short and sorrowful, and there is no healing when a human being dies, and no one has been known to return from Hades.
For we came into being by chance, and afterward we will be as though we had not existed; for the breath in our nostrils is smoke, and reason is a spark in the movement of our heart;
when it is extinguished, the body will become ashes, and the spirit will disperse like insubstantial air.

And our name will be forgotten in time, and no one will remember our works; our life will pass like the traces of a cloud, and will disperse like mist, driven away by the sun’s rays and weighed down by its heat.
For our allotted time is the passing of a shadow, and there is no turning back from our end, because it has been sealed, and no one returns.
Come, then, and let us enjoy the good things that exist, and eagerly make use of creation as in youth.
Let us fill ourselves with costly wine and perfumes, and let no spring blossom pass us by.
Let us crown ourselves with rosebuds before they wither.
Let none of us be without a share in our revelry; let us leave tokens of our enjoyment everywhere, for this is our portion, and this our lot.
Let us oppress the poor righteous person; let us not spare a widow, nor show regard for an old man’s many years of gray hair.
Let our strength be the law of righteousness, for what is weak is shown to be useless.
Let us lie in wait for the righteous person, because he is troublesome to us and opposes our works; he reproaches us for sins against law and charges us with sins against our upbringing.
He professes to have knowledge of God and calls himself a child of the Lord.
He has become a reproach to our thoughts; even the sight of him weighs upon us,
because his life is unlike that of others, and his paths are different.
He has reckoned us counterfeit, and keeps away from our ways as from impurities; he calls the final lot of the righteous blessed, and boasts that God is his father.
Let us see whether his words are true, and test what will happen at his departure.
For if the righteous person is a son of God, He will help him and rescue him from the hand of his opponents.
Let us examine him with insult and torture, so that we may know his gentleness and test his endurance of wrong.
Let us condemn him to a shameful death, for, according to his words, he will be visited with care.”
They reasoned these things and went astray, for their wickedness blinded them;
they did not know the mysteries of God, nor hope for a reward of holiness, nor recognize a prize for blameless souls.
For God created the human being for incorruption and made him an image of His own eternity;
but through the devil’s envy death entered the world, and those who belong to his portion experience it.
But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and torment will surely not touch them.
In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died, and their departure was reckoned a calamity,
and their going away from us a destruction; but they are in peace.
For even if they are punished in the sight of human beings, their hope is full of immortality;
and after being disciplined a little, they will receive great benefits, because God tested them and found them worthy of Himself.
Like gold in a crucible He tested them, and like a sacrificial whole burnt offering He accepted them.
And at the time of their visitation they will shine out, and like sparks among stubble they will dart about.
They will judge nations and rule over peoples, and the Lord will reign over them unto the ages.
Those who trust in Him will understand truth, and the faithful will remain with Him in love, for grace and mercy are for His chosen ones.
But the ungodly will have punishment in keeping with their reasoning— those who neglected what is righteous and departed from the Lord.
For the one who despises wisdom and discipline is wretched; their hope is empty, their labors unprofitable, and their works useless.
Their wives are foolish, and their children wicked; their offspring is accursed.
For blessed is the undefiled barren woman, who has not known a bed of transgression; she will have fruit at the visitation of souls,

and the eunuch who has done no lawless deed with his hand and has not conceived evil against the Lord; for a choice favor will be given him for his faithfulness, and a more delightful portion in the Lord’s temple.
For the fruit of good labors is glorious, and the root of understanding does not fail.
But the children of adulterers will not reach fulfillment, and offspring from an unlawful bed will disappear.
For even if they become long-lived, they will be reckoned as nothing, and their old age will be without honor at the end;
and if they die quickly, they will have no hope, nor consolation on the day of decision.
For the ends of an unrighteous generation are harsh.
Childlessness with virtue is better, for immortality is in its remembrance, because it is recognized both by God and by human beings.
When it is present, people imitate it, and when it has departed, they long for it; throughout the age it marches crowned in triumph, having won the contest for undefiled prizes.
But the prolific multitude of the ungodly will be of no use; from illegitimate shoots it will not send a root deep down, nor establish a secure foundation.
For even if it flourishes in branches for a time, standing insecurely, it will be shaken by wind and uprooted by the force of winds.
Unfulfilled branches will be broken off, and their fruit will be useless, unripe for eating, and fit for nothing.
For children born from unlawful unions are witnesses of wickedness against their parents at their examination.
But if a righteous person dies early, he will be at rest.
For honorable old age is not length of time, nor is it measured by a number of years;
rather, understanding is gray hair for human beings, and an unstained life is the maturity of old age.
Having become pleasing to God, he was loved, and while living among sinners he was transferred.
He was snatched away, lest evil change his understanding or deceit mislead his soul;
for the fascination of wickedness obscures what is good, and the wandering of desire alters an innocent mind.
Having been brought to completion in a short time, he fulfilled long years;
for his soul was pleasing to the Lord; therefore he hastened from the midst of wickedness. Yet the peoples saw and did not understand, nor set such a thing in their minds:
that grace and mercy are among His chosen ones, and visitation among His holy ones.
But a righteous person who has died will condemn the living ungodly, and youth brought swiftly to completion will condemn the many years of an unrighteous person’s old age.
For they will see a wise person’s end and will not understand what the Lord planned concerning him or for what purpose He kept him safe.
They will see and despise, but the Lord will laugh them to scorn.

And afterward they will become a dishonored corpse and an object of outrage among the dead for ever; for He will dash them down headlong, speechless, and shake them from their foundations; they will be laid utterly waste, and will be in anguish, and their remembrance will perish.
They will come in dread at the reckoning of their sins, and their lawless deeds will confront and convict them.
Then the righteous person will stand with great boldness before those who afflicted him and those who disregarded his labors.
When they see him, they will be troubled with terrible fear and astonished at his unexpected salvation.
They will speak among themselves in repentance, and in anguish of spirit they will groan and say:
“This was the one whom we fools once made a laughingstock and a byword of reproach. We reckoned his life madness and his end dishonorable.
How was he counted among the sons of God, and how is his portion among the saints?
So we strayed from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness did not shine upon us, and the sun did not rise upon us.
We were filled with paths of lawlessness and destruction, and traveled through trackless deserts, but the way of the Lord we did not know.
What did arrogance profit us? And what did wealth with boasting contribute to us?
All those things passed like a shadow and like a report rushing by;
like a ship passing through surging water, whose trace cannot be found after it has crossed, nor the path of its keel among the waves;

or like a bird that has flown through the air: no sign of its passage is found. It crossed the light air, lashed by the beat of its pinions and split by the force of its rushing wings; and afterward no sign of its passage was found in it;
or like an arrow shot at a target: the air it cut immediately flowed back into itself, so that its course could not be known:
so we also were born and vanished, and had no sign of virtue to show, but were consumed in our wickedness.”

For the hope of an ungodly person is like dust borne by wind, and like fine frost driven by a storm; like smoke it was dispersed by wind, and like the memory of a guest who stayed one day it passed away.
But the righteous live for ever, and their reward is with the Lord, and the Most High takes care of them.
Therefore they will receive the royal crown of splendor and the diadem of beauty from the Lord’s hand, because with His right hand He will cover them and with His arm He will shield them.
He will take His zeal as full armor and make creation into weapons to repel His enemies;
He will put on righteousness as a breastplate, and put on unfeigned judgment as a helmet;
He will take holiness as an invincible shield,
and sharpen stern wrath into a sword; the world will fight together with Him against the senseless.
Well-aimed bolts of lightning will go forth, and from the clouds, as from a well-curved bow, they will leap at the target;
and hailstones full of fury will be hurled from a catapult; the water of the sea will rage against them, and rivers will flood over them relentlessly.
A mighty wind will oppose them and winnow them away like a storm; lawlessness will lay the whole earth waste, and wrongdoing will overturn the thrones of rulers.
Listen, then, kings, and understand; learn, judges of the ends of the earth.
Give ear, you who rule a multitude and boast over crowds of nations;
for your rule was given you by the Lord, and your authority by the Most High, who will examine your works and search out your plans.
For though you were servants of His kingdom, you did not judge rightly, nor keep law, nor walk according to God’s purpose.
He will come upon you terribly and swiftly, for a severe judgment falls upon those in high position.
For the least is pardonable through mercy, but the powerful will be powerfully examined.
For the Master of all will not shrink before anyone’s face or show deference to greatness, because He Himself made both small and great and provides for all alike;
but a forceful inquiry awaits the mighty.
To you, therefore, rulers, my words are directed, so that you may learn wisdom and not fall away.
For those who keep holy things in holiness will be made holy, and those instructed in them will find a defense.
Desire my words, then; long for them, and you will be instructed.
Wisdom is radiant and unfading; she is readily seen by those who love her and found by those who seek her.
She goes ahead of those who desire her, making herself known first.
The one who rises early for her will not grow weary, for he will find her sitting beside his gates.
For to reflect upon her is the perfection of understanding, and the one who keeps watch for her will soon be free from care;
for she herself goes about seeking those worthy of her, appears graciously to them on their paths, and meets them in every thought.
For her beginning is the truest desire for discipline, and concern for discipline is love;
love is the keeping of her laws, and attention to laws is assurance of incorruption;
and incorruption brings one near to God.
Therefore desire for wisdom leads up to kingship.
If, then, you delight in thrones and scepters, rulers of peoples, honor wisdom, so that you may reign for ever.

What wisdom is and how she came to be, I will declare, and I will not hide mysteries from you; instead I will trace her from the beginning of her origin, and bring the knowledge of her into the open, and I will certainly not pass truth by.
Nor will I travel with wasting envy, for it will have no share with wisdom.
A multitude of wise people is the world’s salvation, and an understanding king is the stability of a people.
Therefore be instructed by my words, and you will benefit.
I too am a mortal human being, equal to all, and a descendant of the first-formed earthborn man; in a mother’s womb I was sculpted into flesh,
taking form in blood over a time of ten months, from a man’s seed and the pleasure that accompanied sleep.
And when I was born, I drew in the common air and fell upon the earth that shares the same lot, crying as my first sound just like everyone else.
I was brought up in swaddling clothes and attentive care.
For no king had a different beginning of birth;
all have one entrance into life, and the same departure.
Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given me; I called out, and a spirit of wisdom came to me.
I preferred her to scepters and thrones, and reckoned wealth as nothing in comparison with her.
Nor did I compare a priceless stone with her, for all gold in her sight is a little sand, and silver will be reckoned as clay before her.
I loved her more than health and beauty, and chose to have her rather than light, because the radiance that comes from her never sleeps.
But all good things came to me together with her, and immeasurable wealth was in her hands.
I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom leads them, but I did not know that she was their mother.
I learned without deceit and share without envy; I do not conceal her wealth.
For she is an unfailing treasure for human beings; those who acquire it enter into friendship with God, commended by the gifts that come from discipline.
May God grant me to speak with judgment and to reflect worthily on what has been given, for He is both the guide of wisdom and the corrector of the wise.
For in His hand are both we and our words, all understanding and skill in crafts.
For He Himself gave me unerring knowledge of existing things: to know the composition of the world and the activity of the elements,
the beginning and end and middle of times, the changes of the solstices and the transitions of seasons,
the cycles of the year and the positions of stars,
the natures of living creatures and the tempers of wild animals, the forces of winds and the reasonings of human beings, the varieties of plants and the powers of roots.
I learned all that is hidden and manifest, for wisdom, the artisan of all things, taught me.
For in her is a spirit intelligent, holy, unique, manifold, subtle, agile, lucid, undefiled, clear, unharmed, loving the good, keen,
unhindered, beneficent, loving humanity, steadfast, secure, free from care, all-powerful, all-overseeing, and passing through all spirits that are intelligent, pure, and most subtle.
For wisdom is more mobile than every motion; she penetrates and passes through all things because of her purity.
For she is a breath of God’s power and a pure outflow of the Almighty’s glory; therefore nothing defiled enters into her.
For she is a radiance of eternal light, an unstained mirror of God’s activity, and an image of His goodness.
Though she is one, she can do all things; remaining in herself, she renews all things, and passing into holy souls from generation to generation, she makes friends of God and prophets.
For God loves no one except the one who dwells with wisdom.
For she is more beautiful than the sun and surpasses every arrangement of stars; compared with light, she is found superior.
For night succeeds light, but evil does not overpower wisdom.
She reaches mightily from end to end, and governs all things well.
I loved her and sought her out from my youth, and sought to take her as my bride, and became a lover of her beauty.
She glorifies her noble birth by sharing life with God, and the Master of all loved her;
for she is initiated into God’s knowledge and is a chooser of His works.
If wealth is a desirable possession in life, what is richer than wisdom, who works all things?
And if understanding accomplishes things, who among existing beings is more skilled than she?
And if anyone loves righteousness, her labors are virtues; for she teaches self-control and understanding, righteousness and courage; nothing in life is more useful for human beings than these.

And if anyone longs for wide experience, she knows ancient things and infers what is to come; she understands turns of speech and solutions of riddles; she knows signs and wonders beforehand, and the outcomes of seasons and times.
Therefore I decided to take her to live with me, knowing that she would be a counselor of good things to me and encouragement amid cares and sorrow.
Through her I will have glory among the crowds, and, though young, honor among elders.
I will be found keen in judgment and will be admired in the sight of rulers.
When I am silent they will wait for me, and when I speak they will pay attention; if I speak at length, they will place a hand upon their mouth.
Through her I will have immortality, and will leave an everlasting remembrance to those after me.
I will govern peoples, and nations will be subjected to me.
Terrifying rulers will fear me when they hear of me; among the multitude I will appear good, and in war courageous.
When I enter my house, I will rest beside her; for companionship with her has no bitterness, and life with her no anguish, but gladness and joy.
Having reasoned these things within myself and considered in my heart that immortality is in kinship with wisdom,

and in friendship with her is good delight, and in the labors of her hands unfailing wealth, and in the shared exercise of companionship with her understanding, and in sharing her words good renown, I went about seeking how to take her to myself.
I was a naturally gifted child, and received a good soul as my lot;
or rather, being good, I came into an undefiled body.

But knowing that I could not otherwise gain possession of her unless God gave her— and this too was understanding: to know whose gift it was— I appealed to the Lord and petitioned Him, and said with my whole heart:
“God of the fathers and Lord of mercy, who made all things by Thy word
and by Thy wisdom fashioned the human being, so that he might rule over the creatures made by Thee
and administer the world in holiness and righteousness, and render judgment in uprightness of soul,
give me wisdom, who sits beside Thy thrones, and do not reject me from among Thy servants.
For I am Thy slave and the son of Thy slave woman, a weak and short-lived human being, deficient in understanding judgment and laws.
For even if someone is perfect among the sons of human beings, without the wisdom that comes from Thee, he will be reckoned as nothing.
Thou didst choose me as king of Thy people and judge of Thy sons and daughters.
Thou didst tell me to build a temple on Thy holy mountain and an altar in the city of Thy dwelling, a likeness of the holy tent that Thou didst prepare beforehand from the beginning.
With Thee is wisdom, who knows Thy works and was present when Thou didst make the world, who understands what is pleasing in Thine eyes and what is upright in Thy commandments.
Send her out from the holy heavens, and from the throne of Thy glory send her, so that she may labor at my side, and I may know what is pleasing to Thee.
For she knows and understands all things, and will guide me prudently in my actions and guard me in her glory;
and my works will be acceptable, and I will judge Thy people righteously and be worthy of my father’s thrones.
For what human being will know God’s purpose? Or who will conceive what the Lord wills?
For the reasonings of mortals are uncertain, and our thoughts precarious;
for a corruptible body weighs down a soul, and the earthly tent burdens a mind full of cares.
With difficulty we infer the things on earth, and find what lies at hand only with labor; but who has traced out the things in heaven?
And who knew Thy purpose, unless Thou didst give wisdom and send Thy Holy Spirit from on high?
And in this way the paths of those on earth were set right, and human beings were taught what pleases Thee, and were saved by wisdom.”
She guarded the first-formed father of the world, who had been created alone, and delivered him from his own transgression;
and she gave him strength to rule over all things.
But an unrighteous man, departing from her in his anger, perished with the passions that made him kill his brother.
Because of him the earth was being flooded, but wisdom again saved it, steering the righteous man by means of humble wood.
When nations were confounded in their shared wickedness, she recognized the righteous man and kept him blameless before God, and preserved him strong against compassion for his child.
When the ungodly were being destroyed, she rescued a righteous man who fled the fire descending upon the Five Cities.
As a witness to its wickedness there still stands a smoking wasteland, and plants whose fruit never reaches ripeness, and a standing pillar of salt, a memorial to a disbelieving soul.

For by passing wisdom by, they were harmed not only by failing to know what is good, but also left life a memorial of their folly, so that even in the things in which they failed they could not escape notice.
But wisdom rescued those who served her from troubles.

She guided a righteous man fleeing his brother’s anger along upright paths; she showed him God’s kingdom and gave him knowledge of holy things; she made him prosper in his hardships and multiplied the fruit of his labors.
She stood beside him against those who overpowered him in their greed, and made him rich.
She guarded him from enemies and kept him safe from those lying in wait; she presided over a mighty contest for him, so that he might know that devotion to God is stronger than everything.
She did not abandon a righteous man who had been sold, but rescued him from sin;

she went down with him into a pit and did not leave him in bonds, until she brought him the scepters of kingship and authority over those who ruled him; she showed those who accused him to be liars and gave him everlasting glory.
She rescued a holy people and blameless offspring from a nation of oppressors;
she entered the soul of a servant of the Lord and opposed terrifying kings with wonders and signs.
She repaid the holy ones the reward of their labors, guided them on a marvelous way, and became for them a covering by day and a flame of stars by night.
She brought them across the Red Sea and led them through abundant water;
but their enemies she overwhelmed with the flood and cast them up from the depth of the abyss.
Therefore the righteous plundered the ungodly and sang hymns, Lord, to Thy holy name, and praised with one accord Thy hand that fought for them;
for wisdom opened the mouth of the mute and made the tongues of infants speak clearly.
She prospered their works by the hand of a holy prophet.
They traveled through an uninhabited desert and pitched tents in trackless places;
they opposed their adversaries and repelled their enemies.
They thirsted and called upon Thee, and water was given them from a sheer rock, and a cure for thirst from hard stone.
For through the very things by which their enemies were punished, they themselves received benefits in their need.
Instead of the source of an ever-flowing river turbid with bloody gore,
as a rebuke to the decree for killing infants, Thou didst give them abundant water beyond their expectation,
showing through the thirst of that time how Thou didst punish their opponents.
For when they were tested, although disciplined in mercy, they learned how the ungodly were tormented when judged in wrath.
For these Thou didst test as a father giving instruction, but those Thou didst examine as a stern king condemning them.
Whether absent or present, they were worn down alike;
for a twofold sorrow seized them, and a groaning at the remembrance of what had passed.
For when they heard that the others had received benefits through their own punishments, they became aware of the Lord.
For the one long ago cast out in exposure, whom they rejected with mockery, they marveled at in the final outcome, having thirsted unlike the righteous.

In return for the senseless reasonings of their unrighteousness, in which they went astray and worshiped irrational creeping things and worthless beasts, Thou didst send upon them a multitude of irrational animals for vengeance,
so that they might know that through the things by which someone sins, through those things he is punished.
For Thine all-powerful hand, which created the world from unformed matter, was not at a loss to send upon them a multitude of bears or fierce lions,
or newly created, unknown beasts full of fury, either breathing a fire-breathing blast, or scattering a stench of smoke, or flashing dreadful sparks from their eyes,
whose injury could not only utterly crush them, but whose very appearance could terrify and destroy them.
Even without these, they could have fallen at a single breath, pursued by justice and winnowed away by the breath of Thy power; but Thou didst arrange all things by measure and number and weight.
For great strength is always at Thy disposal, and who will oppose the might of Thine arm?
For the whole world before Thee is like a slight tipping of the scales, and like a drop of morning dew that has fallen upon the earth.
But Thou hast mercy on all, because Thou canst do all things, and Thou overlookest human sins with a view to repentance.
For Thou lovest all existing things and abhorrest nothing that Thou didst make; for Thou wouldst not have fashioned anything while hating it.
How could anything have endured unless Thou didst will it, or what had not been called by Thee have been preserved?
But Thou sparest all things, because they are Thine, Master who loves life.
For Thine incorruptible Spirit is in all things.
Therefore Thou reprovest those who fall away little by little, and admonishest them by reminding them of the things in which they sin, so that, freed from evil, they may believe in Thee, Lord.
For the ancient inhabitants of Thy holy land,
whom Thou didst hate for practicing the most detestable things— works of sorcery and unholy rites,
merciless murders of children, and an entrail-devouring feast of human flesh and blood— initiates from the midst of a ritual company,
and parents who were murderers of helpless lives, Thou didst will to destroy by the hands of our fathers,
so that the land most precious to Thee of all might receive a worthy settlement of God’s children.
Yet even these Thou didst spare as human beings, and send hornets as forerunners of Thine army, so that they might destroy them little by little.
Thou wast not unable to give the ungodly into the hands of the righteous in battle, or to crush them all at once with terrifying beasts or a stern word;
but judging them little by little, Thou didst give room for repentance, not unaware that their origin was wicked, and their evil ingrained, and that their reasoning would never change.
For they were an accursed offspring from the beginning; nor was it out of fear of anyone that Thou didst grant them respite for their sins.

For who will say, ‘What hast Thou done?’ Or who will oppose Thy judgment? Who will accuse Thee concerning destroyed nations that Thou didst make? Or who will come to confront Thee as an avenger concerning unrighteous human beings?
For there is no god besides Thee, who cares for all, so that Thou shouldst have to show that Thou hast not judged unjustly;
nor will a king or ruler be able to face Thee concerning those Thou didst punish.
But being righteous, Thou administerest all things righteously, regarding it as alien to Thy power to condemn anyone who does not deserve punishment.
For Thy strength is the beginning of righteousness, and Thy mastery over all makes Thee spare all.
For Thou displayest strength when the completeness of Thy power is disbelieved, and among those who know, Thou exposest their audacity.
But Thou, master of strength, judgest with gentleness and governest us with great forbearance; for the ability to act is at Thy disposal whenever Thou wilt.
Through such works Thou didst teach Thy people that the righteous person must love humanity, and make Thy sons hopeful, because Thou givest repentance for sins.
For if Thou didst punish the enemies of Thy children, who were liable to death, with such attention and leniency, giving times and room through which they might be freed from evil,
with how much care didst Thou judge Thy sons, to whose fathers Thou didst give oaths and covenants of good promises?
Therefore, while disciplining us, Thou scourgest our enemies with myriad blows, so that when judging we may consider Thy goodness, and when judged we may expect mercy.
Therefore those who lived unrighteously in a foolish way of life Thou didst also torment through their own abominations.
For they wandered even farther than the paths of error, supposing that creatures despised even among shameful animals were gods, deceived like senseless infants.
Therefore, as to children without reason, Thou didst send judgment in mockery.
But those who were not admonished by playful reproofs will experience a judgment worthy of God.

For as they suffered punishment through the very creatures they had supposed to be gods, they grew indignant at them, and saw and recognized as the true God the One they had long refused to know; therefore the final condemnation also came upon them.

For all human beings in whom ignorance of God was present were futile by nature; from the good things seen they could not know the One who is, nor, attending to the works, did they recognize the Artisan.
Instead, they supposed fire or wind or swift-moving air, or the circuit of stars or violent water, or the lights of heaven to be gods, rulers of the world.
If, delighted by their beauty, they supposed these things to be gods, let them know how much better than these their Master is; for the Originator of beauty created them.
And if they were astonished at their power and activity, let them understand from these how much more powerful the One who fashioned them is.
For from the greatness and beauty of created things their Maker is seen by analogy.
Yet the blame upon these is small, for perhaps they themselves go astray while seeking God and wishing to find Him.
For living among His works, they search them out and are persuaded by their appearance, because the things seen are beautiful.
But again, even they are not excusable;
for if they were able to know so much that they could investigate the world, how did they not more quickly find the Master of these things?

But wretched are those whose hopes rest in dead things, who called the works of human hands gods: gold and silver, exercises of craftsmanship, likenesses of living creatures, or a useless stone, the work of an ancient hand.
Suppose a woodcutting craftsman sawed down a manageable tree, skillfully scraped off all its bark, and, working it handsomely, fashioned a useful vessel for the service of life,
and burned the scraps from the work to prepare food and ate his fill,

then took the scrap left from these, useful for nothing, a crooked piece of wood grown full of knots, and carved it with the care of his leisure, shaped it with practiced understanding, and made it resemble a human image,
or made it like some worthless animal, coating it with red ocher and reddening its surface with paint, and covering every blemish in it,
and made for it a dwelling worthy of it, set it in a wall, and secured it with iron.
He took care that it would not fall, knowing that it cannot help itself; for it is an image and needs help.
Yet when praying concerning his possessions, marriage, and children, he is not ashamed to address what has no soul; for health he calls upon what is weak,
for life he petitions what is dead, for assistance he begs what is utterly inexperienced, for a journey what cannot even use its feet,
and for gain, work, and success of his hands, he asks vigor of what is most powerless with its hands.
Again, someone preparing for a voyage and about to traverse wild waves calls upon a piece of wood more rotten than the ship carrying him.
For the desire for gain devised that ship, and wisdom, the artisan, fashioned it;
but Thy providence, Father, steers it, for Thou didst give a way even in the sea and a safe path among the waves,
showing that Thou canst save from every danger, so that even someone without skill may embark.

Thou wilt that the works of Thy wisdom should not be idle; therefore human beings entrust their lives even to a very small piece of wood, and, crossing the surge on a raft, they were brought safely through.
For even at the beginning, when arrogant giants were perishing, the hope of the world took refuge on a raft and left to the age a seed for generation, steered by Thy hand.
For blessed is wood through which righteousness comes about;
but the handmade object is accursed, both it and its maker: the one because he made it, and the other because, though corruptible, it was named a god.
For equally hateful to God are the ungodly person and his ungodliness;
for what was done will be punished together with the one who did it.
Therefore there will also be a visitation upon the nations’ idols, because within God’s creation they became an abomination, stumbling blocks to human souls, and a snare for the feet of fools.
For the devising of idols is the beginning of sexual immorality, and their invention the corruption of life.
For they did not exist from the beginning, nor will they exist for ever;
through human vainglory they entered the world, and therefore a swift end was planned for them.

For a father worn down by untimely grief, having made an image of a child swiftly taken away, now honored as a god the one who had once been a dead human being, and handed on mysteries and rites to those under him.
Then, strengthened over time, the ungodly custom was kept as law.

And carved images were worshiped at rulers’ commands; when people could not honor them face to face because they lived far away, they reproduced their distant appearance and made a visible image of the honored king, so that by their zeal they might flatter the absent one as though present.
The artist’s ambition urged even those who did not know the king toward still greater worship;
for, perhaps wishing to please the ruler, he used his art to force the likeness toward greater beauty.
The multitude, drawn by the charm of the workmanship, now reckoned as an object of worship the human being whom they had honored a little before.
And this became an ambush for life, because human beings, enslaved either to misfortune or to royal power, bestowed upon stones and pieces of wood the name that cannot be shared.
Then it was not enough to go astray about the knowledge of God; living in the great war of ignorance, they also call such great evils peace.
For while celebrating rites that murder children, or secret mysteries, or frenzied revelries with strange customs,
they no longer keep either lives or marriages pure; one kills another by ambush or grieves him by adultery.
Bloodshed and murder, theft and deceit, hold everything in confusion, corruption, unfaithfulness, disturbance, perjury,
confusion of good things, forgetfulness of favor, defilement of souls, alteration of natural relations, disorder in marriages, adultery, and licentiousness.
For worship of nameless idols is the beginning, cause, and end of every evil.
For they either go mad in their merrymaking, or prophesy lies, or live unjustly, or readily swear falsely.
For trusting in lifeless idols, they do not expect to be harmed when they swear wrongly.
But just consequences will pursue them for both things: because they thought wrongly about God by attending to idols, and swore unjustly in deceit, despising holiness.
For it is not the power of those by whom they swear, but the justice due to sinners, that always pursues the transgression of the unrighteous.
But Thou, our God, art good and true, patient, and governing all things in mercy.
For even if we sin, we are Thine, knowing Thy might; but we will not sin, knowing that we have been reckoned as Thine.
For to know Thee is complete righteousness, and to know Thy might is the root of immortality.
For neither the evil-devising invention of human beings misled us, nor the fruitless labor of painters, a form stained with varied colors,
the sight of which stirs desire in fools, and one longs for the breathless form of a dead image.
Lovers of evil and worthy of such hopes are those who make them, those who desire them, and those who worship them.

For a potter, laboriously kneading soft earth, shapes each object for our service; from the same clay he fashioned alike vessels serving clean purposes and those serving the opposite; and the clay-worker decides the use of each kind.

With evil labor he also shapes a futile god from the same clay, though he himself, having come from earth a little before, will shortly go back to that from which he was taken, when the debt of his soul is demanded.

But his concern is not that he is about to die, nor that his life is short; instead, he competes with goldsmiths and silver-workers, imitates bronze-workers, and considers it glory that he fashions counterfeits.
His heart is ashes, and his hope more worthless than earth, and his life more dishonorable than clay,
because he did not know the One who formed him, who breathed into him an active soul and breathed in a life-giving spirit.
Instead, they reckoned our life a plaything and our existence a profitable fair; for he says that one must make gain from whatever source, even evil.
For this man knows better than everyone that he is sinning, when he crafts fragile vessels and carved images from earthy material.
But all the enemies of Thy people who oppressed them are most foolish and more wretched than an infant’s soul,

because they also reckoned all the nations’ idols gods, though these have neither use of eyes for sight, nor nostrils for drawing in air, nor ears to hear, nor fingers of their hands to feel, and their feet are idle for walking.
For a human being made them, and one who had borrowed his spirit fashioned them; for no human being can shape a god like himself.
Being mortal, he makes a dead thing with lawless hands; for he is better than the objects he worships: he at least has lived, but they never have.
They also worship the most hateful animals, for compared in senselessness with the others, these are worse;
Nor, in their appearance as animals, are they beautiful enough to be desired, and they have escaped both God’s praise and His blessing.
Therefore they were deservedly punished through similar creatures and tormented by a multitude of beasts.
In contrast to that punishment, Thou didst benefit Thy people: to meet their eager appetite Thou didst prepare quail as food, a novel taste,

so that those, though desiring food, would turn away even from their necessary appetite because of the loathsomeness of the creatures sent upon them, while these, after a brief lack, would share in a novel taste.
For unavoidable need had to come upon those who oppressed, but these only had to be shown how their enemies were tormented.
For even when the terrible fury of beasts came upon them, and they were being destroyed by the bites of twisting snakes, Thy wrath did not remain to the end;
they were troubled for a short time as an admonition, having a symbol of salvation to remind them of the commandment of Thy law.
For the one who turned toward it was saved not through what was seen, but through Thee, the Savior of all.
Through this Thou didst also convince our enemies that Thou art the One who rescues from every evil.
For the bites of locusts and flies killed those others, and no cure was found for their lives, because they deserved to be punished by such creatures;
but even the teeth of venom-spitting serpents did not conquer Thy sons, for Thy mercy came to meet them and healed them.
For they were stung as a reminder of Thine oracles and swiftly brought safely through, so that they would not fall into deep forgetfulness and become inattentive to Thy beneficence.
For neither herb nor poultice healed them, but Thy word, Lord, which heals all.
For Thou hast authority over life and death, and Thou bringest down to the gates of Hades and bringest up again;
but a human being kills by his wickedness, and does not bring back a spirit that has gone out, nor release a soul that has been taken.
But it is impossible to escape Thy hand.
For the ungodly, refusing to know Thee, were scourged by the strength of Thine arm, pursued by strange rains, hail, and relentless showers, and consumed by fire.
Most astonishingly, in water that quenches everything, the fire worked still more strongly, for the world fights for the righteous.
At one time the flame was tamed, so that it would not burn up the animals sent against the ungodly, but they themselves, seeing, would know that they were being driven by God’s judgment;
at another time, even amid water, it burns beyond fire’s own power, so that it may destroy the produce of an unrighteous land.
In contrast, Thou didst feed Thy people with angels’ food and supply them ready bread from heaven without toil, capable of every delight and suited to every taste.
For Thy sustenance manifested Thy sweetness toward Thy children; serving the desire of the one who received it, it was transformed into whatever that person wished.
Snow and ice endured fire and did not melt, so that they might know that the enemies’ fruits were destroyed by fire blazing in the hail and flashing in the rains;
yet again, so that the righteous might be nourished, this fire has even forgotten its own power.
For creation, serving Thee who made it, strains itself for punishment against the unrighteous and relaxes itself for benefit on behalf of those who trust in Thee.
Therefore at that time also, changing into all things, it served Thy gift that nourishes all, according to the desire of those in need,
so that Thy sons whom Thou didst love, Lord, might learn that it is not the production of fruits that nourishes a human being, but Thine utterance that preserves those who trust in Thee.
For what was not destroyed by fire melted when merely warmed by a brief ray of the sun,
so that it might be known that one must rise before the sun to give Thee thanks and appeal to Thee at the rising of the light.
For the hope of an ungrateful person will melt like wintry frost and flow away like useless water.
For Thy judgments are great and hard to recount; therefore uninstructed souls went astray.
For lawless people, supposing they could oppress a holy nation, lay as prisoners of darkness and captives of a long night, shut under their roofs, fugitives from eternal providence.
For thinking they could escape notice in secret sins, under a lightless covering of forgetfulness, they were scattered, terribly astonished and shaken by apparitions.
For not even the recess that held them kept them free from fear; terrifying sounds rang around them, and gloomy specters with unsmiling faces appeared.
No force of fire could give light, nor could the bright flames of stars endure to illuminate that hateful night.
Only a self-kindled fire full of fear shone through to them; terrified by that unseen sight, they reckoned what they saw still worse.
The delusions of magical art lay prostrate, and its boasting of understanding suffered a scornful exposure;
for those who promised to drive away the terrors and disturbances of a sick soul were themselves sick with a ridiculous fear.

For even if nothing disturbing frightened them, startled by the passing of beasts and the hissing of creeping things, they perished trembling, refusing even to look at the air, which cannot be escaped anywhere.
For wickedness is a cowardly thing, condemned by its own witness; pressed by conscience, it always imagines grievous things.
For fear is nothing but a betrayal of the aids that come from reasoning;
and as expectation within grows weaker, it reckons ignorance more fearful than the cause that produces the torment.
But they, sleeping the same sleep during that truly powerless night, which had come upon them from the recesses of powerless Hades,
were at one moment driven by monstrous apparitions, at another paralyzed by their soul’s betrayal; for a sudden and unexpected fear poured over them.
Then whoever it might be who fell there was held under guard, shut in a prison without iron bars.
For whether someone was a farmer or shepherd or a laborer toiling in the wilderness, once overtaken, he endured the inescapable compulsion; for all were bound by one chain of darkness.
Whether a whistling wind, or the melodious sound of birds among spreading branches, or the rhythm of water rushing violently, or the harsh crash of falling rocks,
or the unseen running of leaping animals, or the voice of the fiercest roaring beasts, or an echo rebounding from the hollows of mountains, these terrified and paralyzed them.
For the whole world was illuminated by brilliant light and occupied with unhindered works;
but over those alone a heavy night was spread, an image of the darkness that was to receive them; yet they were heavier to themselves than the darkness.
But for Thy holy ones there was very great light; hearing their voices but not seeing their forms, the others called them blessed because they had not suffered likewise,
and thanked them because, though previously wronged, they did not harm them, and begged pardon for their quarrel.
In contrast, Thou didst supply a fire-blazing pillar, a guide for an unknown journey, and a harmless sun for a glorious sojourn abroad.
For those deserved to be deprived of light and imprisoned in darkness who had kept Thy sons shut up, through whom the incorruptible light of law was to be given to the world.

When they planned to kill the infants of the holy ones, and one child had been exposed and saved, Thou didst take away their multitude of children as a rebuke and destroy them together in violent water.
That night was known beforehand to our fathers, so that, knowing securely the oaths in which they trusted, they might take courage.
Thy people awaited the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of enemies;
for by the very means through which Thou didst punish the opponents, Thou didst glorify us, calling us to Thyself.

For in secret the holy children of good ancestors offered sacrifice, and in unity established the divine law: that the saints would share alike in the same good things and dangers, already singing beforehand the praises of the fathers.
But the discordant cry of enemies echoed back, and a pitiful sound spread abroad as children were mourned.
Slave and master were punished together by the same judgment, and the commoner suffered the same things as the king;
all together, under one name of death, they had countless dead; for the living were not even sufficient to bury them, since in a single moment their most honored offspring had been destroyed.
For though they disbelieved everything because of their sorceries, at the destruction of the firstborn they acknowledged that the people were God’s son.
For while quiet silence surrounded all things and night was midway through its swift course,
Thine all-powerful word leaped from heaven, from royal thrones, a stern warrior, into the midst of the doomed land, carrying Thine unfeigned command as a sharp sword;
standing there, it filled all things with death; it touched heaven while standing upon the earth.
Then at once apparitions of dreadful dreams disturbed them, and unexpected fears came upon them;
one here and another there, hurled down half-dead, made known the reason why they were dying.
For the dreams that troubled them had announced this beforehand, so that they would not perish without knowing why they suffered.
But a trial of death touched the righteous too, and a breaking of the multitude occurred in the wilderness; yet the wrath did not remain long.

For a blameless man hastened to fight for them, bringing the weapon of his own ministry: prayer and propitiation by incense. He opposed the wrath and put an end to the calamity, showing that he was Thy servant.
He conquered the anger, not by bodily strength, not by the activity of weapons, but by a word he subdued the punisher, reminding him of the fathers’ oaths and covenants.
For when the dead had already fallen in heaps upon one another, he stood between them and checked the wrath, and cut off the path to the living.
For upon his ankle-length garment was the whole world, and the glories of the fathers upon the engraving of four rows of stones, and Thy majesty upon the diadem of his head.
To these the destroyer yielded, and these he feared; for the trial of wrath alone was enough.
But merciless fury came upon the ungodly to the end, for He knew beforehand even what they would do,
that after permitting the people to depart and sending them on their way with haste, they would change their minds and pursue them.

For while their griefs were still at hand and they were lamenting beside the graves of the dead, they drew upon themselves another senseless plan, and pursued as fugitives those whom they had begged to leave.
For the compulsion they deserved drew them toward this end and cast upon them forgetfulness of what had happened, so that they might fill up the punishment still lacking in their torments,
and Thy people might experience an astonishing journey, while those others found an extraordinary death.
For the whole creation, in its own kind, was being fashioned anew from the beginning, serving Thy commands, so that Thy children might be guarded unharmed.
The cloud overshadowing the camp was seen, and dry land rising from water that had existed before, an unobstructed way out of the Red Sea, and a grass-bearing plain out of the violent surge;
through it those sheltered by Thy hand passed as an entire nation, having seen marvelous wonders.
For they grazed like horses and leaped like lambs, praising Thee, Lord, who rescued them.
For they still remembered the things from their sojourn: how, instead of producing animals, the earth brought forth gnats, and instead of aquatic creatures the river disgorged a multitude of frogs.
Later they also saw a new production of birds, when, urged on by desire, they asked for luxurious foods;
for as a consolation quail came up to them from the sea.

Punishments also came upon the sinners, not without earlier signs in the violence of thunderbolts; for they suffered justly for their own wickedness, since they had practiced a harsher hatred of strangers.
For the former did not receive unfamiliar visitors when they came, but these enslaved strangers who had benefited them.
And not only that: there will be a visitation upon the former, since they received foreigners with hostility;
but the latter, after receiving with celebrations those who had already shared in the same rights, afflicted them with terrible labors.
They were also struck with blindness, like those at the righteous man’s doors, when, surrounded by yawning darkness, each sought the passage through his own doors.

For the elements were being rearranged among themselves, as notes on a harp change the pattern of the rhythm, while always retaining their sound; this can be inferred precisely from observing what happened.
For land creatures were changed into water creatures, and swimming creatures moved onto land;
fire in water exceeded its own power, and water forgot its nature of extinguishing;
flames, conversely, did not wither the flesh of perishable animals walking among them, nor the meltable, crystal-like kind of heavenly food that readily melts.
For in every way, Lord, Thou didst magnify and glorify Thy people, and didst not disregard them, standing beside them at every time and place.
With what shall I take hold of the Lord and grasp my God Most High? Shall I take hold of Him with whole burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
Will the Lord receive with thousands of rams or with ten thousands of fat-rich torrents? Shall I give my firstborn offspring for impieties, the fruit of my body for the sin of my life?
Has it been declared to you, O man, what is good? Or what does the Lord seek from you, except to do justice, and to love mercy, and to be ready to walk with the Lord your God?
You shall fear the Lord your God, and you shall serve Him, and you shall cleave unto Him, and you shall swear by His name.
You shall not go after other gods, of the gods of the nations round about you,
for the Lord your God in the midst of you is a jealous God; lest the Lord your God be kindled to wrath against you, and destroy you from the face of the earth.
You shall not put the Lord your God to the test, as you tested Him at Testing.
You shall diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God, the testimonies and the ordinances which He commanded you.
And you shall do that which is pleasing and good before the Lord your God, that it may be well with you, and that you may enter and inherit the good land which the Lord sware unto your fathers,
Is the Lord’s hand unable to save? Or has His ear grown heavy so that He cannot hear?
Instead, your offenses stand between you and God, and because of your sins He has turned His face away from you so as not to show mercy.
For your hands are stained with blood and your fingers with sins. Your lips spoke lawlessness, and your tongue meditates on injustice.
No one speaks what is just, nor is there true judgment. They trust vain things and speak emptiness, for they conceive trouble and give birth to lawlessness.
Therefore, putting away falsehood, let each speak truth with his neighbor, because we are members of one another.
Be angry and do not sin. Do not let the sun go down upon your anger,
nor give a place to the devil.
Let the one who steals steal no longer, but rather let him labor, doing what is good with his own hands, so that he may have something to share with the one in need.
Let no rotten word come out of your mouth, but only what is good for building up as needed, so that it may give grace to those who hear.
And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
Let all bitterness and rage and anger and shouting and slander be taken away from you, with all malice.
But be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, just as God in Christ forgave you.
The heart is deep beyond all things, and so is a human; and who will know him?
I, the Lord, examine hearts and test kidneys, to give each according to his ways and the fruits of his practices.
A partridge called; it gathered what it did not bear. One makes his wealth without judgment; in the middle of his days they will abandon him, and at his last he will be foolish.
For the end. A psalm for David. Lord, Thou didst test me and know me.
Thou knewest my sitting and my rising; Thou didst understand my reasonings from afar.
Thou didst trace my path and my measuring cord, and Thou didst foresee all my ways.
For there is no word on my tongue,
behold, Lord, Thou knewest all things, the last and the first; Thou didst form me and place Thy hand upon me.
Thy knowledge was made wondrous beyond me; it grew strong—I cannot reach it.
Where can I go from Thy Spirit, and where can I flee from Thy face?
If I ascend to heaven, Thou art there; if I descend into Hades, Thou art present.
if I take up my wings at dawn and settle at the sea’s farthest reaches,
indeed, even there Thy hand will guide me, and Thy right hand will hold me fast.
And I said, “Then darkness will trample me, and night is light in my delight.”
For darkness will not be dark from Thee, and night will be lit up like day; as its darkness, so also its light.
Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten; for the tree is known by the fruit.
Brood of vipers! How can you speak good things when you are evil? For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
The good person brings forth good things from the good treasure, and the evil person brings forth evil things from the evil treasure.
But I tell you that people will give account on the day of judgment for every idle word they speak.
For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
How long with this evil congregation? They grumble before Me; I have heard the sons of Israel’s grumbling that they have directed against you.
Say to them, I live, says the Lord: I will certainly do to you just as you have spoken into My ears.
In this wilderness your bodies shall fall, with your entire registration and those of you counted from twenty years old and upward who grumbled against Me.
You shall certainly not enter the land over which I stretched out My hand to settle you upon it, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
I will judge you, each according to his way, house of Israel, says the Lord. Turn back and turn away from all your impieties, and they will not become a punishment of injustice for you.
Cast away from yourselves all your impieties with which you acted impiously against Me, and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why are you dying, house of Israel?
For I do not desire the death of the one who dies, says the Lord.”

And God said, “Let Us make man in Our image and likeness; and let them rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of heaven, the cattle, all the earth, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.”
And God made man; in the image of God He made him; male and female He made them.

And God blessed them, saying, “Grow and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of heaven, all the cattle, all the earth, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.”
And God said, “Behold, I have given you every plant sowing seed upon all the earth, and every tree that bears fruit containing seed. These shall be yours for food.
And to every wild beast of the earth, every bird of heaven, and every creeping thing upon the earth that has life within it, I have given every green plant for food.” And it was so.
And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning: a sixth day.
In ways of righteousness is life, but the ways of those who remember wrongs lead to death.
Therefore hear the Lord’s word, afflicted men and rulers of this people in Jerusalem:
Because you said, “We made a covenant with Hades and agreements with death; if a rushing storm passes, it will certainly not come upon us. We made falsehood our hope and will be sheltered by deceit,”
therefore thus says the Lord: “Behold, I will place in Zion’s foundations a costly, chosen, precious cornerstone, in her foundations, and whoever trusts in it will certainly not be ashamed.
I will make judgment a hope, and My mercy will be weights; those trusting deceit do so in vain, for a storm will certainly not pass you by—
might it also remove your covenant with death? Your hope toward Hades will certainly not remain. If a rushing storm comes, you will become its trampling ground.
“For a mortal born of woman is short-lived and full of wrath.
Like a flower that blossomed, he fell away; he fled like a shadow and will not remain.
Didst Thou not take account of this one also, and bring him into judgment before Thee?
For who will be clean from filth? No one.
Even if his life on earth is one day, his months are numbered with Thee; Thou didst set a time, and he will certainly not go beyond it.
Leave him alone so that he may be quiet and take pleasure in life like a hired worker.
For a tree has hope: if it is cut down, it will blossom again, and its shoot will not fail.
For even if its root grows old in earth and its trunk dies in rock,
from the scent of water it will blossom and produce a harvest like a newly planted tree.
But a man who has died is gone; a mortal who has fallen is no more.
For in time a sea diminishes, and a river, left desolate, dries up.
But a person who lies down will certainly not rise until heaven is no longer stitched together; they will not wake from their sleep.

when they look from a height and terrors are on the road, when the almond blossoms, the locust grows fat and the caperberry is scattered; for the human being went to his everlasting home, and mourners circled in the marketplace;
before the silver cord is overturned, the golden flower ornament is crushed, the jar is broken at the spring and the wheel runs together at the pit;
and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
Remember, then, that my life is a breath, and my eye will no longer return to see good.
The eye of the one who sees me will no longer look upon me; Thine eyes will be upon me, and I will be no more,
like a cloud cleared away from heaven. For if a person goes down to Hades, he will never come up again,
nor will he ever return again to his own house, nor will his place recognize him any longer.
The Lord Sabaoth called on that day for weeping, lamentation, shaving and putting on sackcloth,
but they made gladness and exultation, slaughtering calves and sacrificing sheep to eat meat and drink wine, saying, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”
These things are revealed in the Lord Sabaoth’s ears: “This sin will not be forgiven you until you die.”
Woe to those rising in the morning and pursuing strong drink, lingering into the evening, for wine will burn them up!
For with lyre and harp, drums and flutes they drink wine, but they do not look at the Lord’s works or consider the works of His hands.
Therefore My people became captive because they did not know the Lord, and there was a multitude of dead through famine and thirst for water.
Woe to the crown of insolence, Ephraim’s hired men; the flower fallen from glory on the summit of the fertile mountain, those drunk without wine!
Behold, the Lord’s wrath is strong and harsh, like falling hail with no covering, falling violently. Like a great mass of water dragging a country, He will give the land rest with His hands.
Underfoot will be trampled the crown of insolence, Ephraim’s hired men.
The flower fallen from the hope of glory, on the high mountain’s summit, will be like an early fig: whoever sees it will want to swallow it before taking it into his hand.
And you shall not ill-treat a resident foreigner, neither shall you afflict him; for you were resident foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You shall not mistreat any widow or orphan.
But if you afflict them, and they cry aloud to Me, I will surely listen to their voice,
I will be angry with wrath and kill you with the sword. Your wives will become widows and your children orphans.
And if you lend silver to your poor brother beside you, you shall not press him hard, neither shall you lay interest upon him.
And if you take your neighbour’s garment in pledge, you shall restore it to him before the setting of the sun;
for this is his covering, his only garment for his nakedness; What shall he sleep in? If therefore he cries to Me, I will listen to him; for I am merciful.
They became people planning troubles and working evil on their beds, and at daybreak they carried them out, because they did not raise their hands to God.
They coveted fields and plundered orphans, oppressed houses and plundered a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.
The sinner will watch the righteous closely and gnash his teeth at him.
But the Lord will laugh him to scorn, for He foresees that his day will come.
The sinners drew a sword and stretched their bow, to cast down the poor and needy, to slaughter the upright in heart.
May their sword enter their own heart, and may their bows be shattered.
But Jesus answered them, “My Father is working even now, and I am working.”
For this reason, therefore, the Jews sought all the more to kill Him, because He not only broke the Sabbath, but also called God His own Father, making Himself equal to God.
They hated one who reproved at the gates and abhorred a holy word.

Therefore, because you struck the poor with fists and accepted choice gifts from them, you built houses of polished stone but certainly will not inhabit them; you planted desirable vineyards but certainly will not drink their wine.
For I knew your many impieties, and your sins are strong: trampling the righteous, taking payments and turning aside the poor at the gates.
Therefore the understanding person will be silent at that time, because it is an evil time.
Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly, and did not stand in the way of sinners, and did not sit in the seat of pestilent men;
but his will is in the Lord’s law, and on His law he will meditate day and night.
He will be like the tree planted beside the outlets of waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and whose leaf will not fall off; and everything he does will be prospered.
Not so the ungodly, not so, but like chaff which the wind flings away from the face of the earth.
Therefore the ungodly will not rise in judgment, nor sinners in the council of the righteous;
for the Lord knows the way of the righteous, and the way of the ungodly will perish.
Do not become unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what sharing is there between righteousness and lawlessness, or what fellowship between light and darkness?
And what harmony is there between Christ and Beliar, or what portion does a believer have with an unbeliever?

And what agreement is there between God’s temple and idols? For we are the temple of the living God, just as God said: “I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.
Therefore come out from their midst and be separated, says the Lord, and do not touch anything unclean; and I will receive you.
And I will be a Father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to Me, says the Lord Almighty.”
Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort around Him.
They stripped Him and put a scarlet cloak around Him.
They wove a crown from thorns, placed it upon His head, and put a reed in His right hand. Kneeling before Him, they mocked Him, saying, “Greetings, King of the Jews!”
They spat on Him, took the reed, and kept striking Him upon the head.
After mocking Him, they stripped off the cloak, dressed Him in His own garments, and led Him away to crucify Him.
As they went out, they found a Cyrenian man named Simon. They compelled him to carry His cross.
They came to a place called Golgotha, which is called Place of a Skull,
and gave Him wine mixed with gall to drink. After tasting it, He was unwilling to drink.
After crucifying Him, they divided His garments by casting a lot,
and sat there keeping watch over Him.
Above His head they placed the written charge against Him: “This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.”
Then two robbers were crucified with Him, one at His right and one at His left.
Those passing by reviled Him, shaking their heads
and saying, “Thou who destroyest the sanctuary and buildest it in three days, save Thyself! If Thou art God’s Son, come down from the cross.”
Likewise the chief priests, mocking with the scribes and elders, said,
“He saved others; Himself He cannot save. He is King of Israel! Let Him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in Him.
He trusts in God; let Him rescue Him now, if He desires Him, for He said, ‘I am God’s Son.’”
The robbers crucified with Him also reproached Him in the same way.
From the sixth hour darkness came upon all the land until the ninth hour.
And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” That is, “My God, My God, why hast Thou forsaken Me?”
Some standing there heard and said, “This Man is calling Elijah.”
Immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, placed it on a reed, and gave Him a drink.
But the rest said, “Leave it; let us see whether Elijah comes to save Him.”
Jesus again cried out with a loud voice and released His spirit.
So I say this and testify in the Lord: you must no longer walk as the Gentiles also walk, in the futility of their mind,
being darkened in understanding, alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance in them, because of the hardness of their heart.
Having become unfeeling, they handed themselves over to licentiousness for the practice of every impurity in greed.

Now the serpent was more cunning than all the wild beasts upon the earth that the Lord God had made. And the serpent said to the woman, “Why has God said, ‘You shall not eat from any tree in the garden’?”
And the woman said to the serpent, “We may eat of the fruit of the trees in the garden.
But of the fruit of the tree in the midst of the garden, God said, ‘You shall not eat of it, nor shall you touch it, lest you die.’”
And the serpent said to the woman, “You shall surely not die.
For God knew that on the day you ate of it, your eyes would be opened, and you would be as gods, knowing good and evil.”
And the woman saw that the tree was good for food, pleasing to the eyes, and beautiful to contemplate. And she took of its fruit and ate; she also gave some to her husband with her, and they ate.
And the eyes of both were opened, and they knew that they were naked. And they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.
And they heard the sound of the Lord God walking in the garden toward evening. And Adam and his wife hid themselves from the face of the Lord God among the trees of the garden.
And the Lord God called to Adam and said to him, “Adam, where are you?”
And he said to Him, “I heard Thy voice as Thou didst walk in the garden, and I was afraid because I am naked, and I hid myself.”
And He said to him, “Who told you that you are naked? Have you eaten from the tree of which alone I commanded you not to eat?”
And Adam said, “The woman whom Thou didst give to be with me—she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate.”
And the Lord God said to the woman, “What is this you have done?” And the woman said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”

And the Lord God said to the serpent: Because you have done this, cursed are you above all cattle and all the wild beasts of the earth. Upon your breast and belly you shall go, and earth you shall eat all the days of your life.
And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He shall watch for your head, and you shall watch for his heel.
And to the woman He said: I will greatly multiply your sorrows and your groaning; in sorrow you shall bear children. You shall turn toward your husband, and he shall rule over you.

And to Adam He said: Because you listened to the voice of your wife and ate from the tree of which alone I commanded you not to eat, cursed is the earth in your labours; in pain you shall eat of it all the days of your life.
Thorns and thistles it shall bring forth for you, and you shall eat the plants of the field.
By the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread, until you return to the earth from which you were taken; for earth you are, and unto earth you shall return.
A psalm for Asaph. God stood in an assembly of gods, and in their midst He judges gods:
“How long do you judge injustice and favor sinners? Diapsalma.
Judge for the fatherless and the poor; vindicate the lowly and the needy.
Deliver the needy and the poor; rescue them from the hand of a sinner.”
They did not know or understand; they pass through darkness; all the foundations of the earth will be shaken.
“I said, ‘You are gods, and all sons of the Most High.’
But you die like human beings, and fall like one of the rulers.”
Rise, God, judge the earth, for Thou wilt take inheritance among all the nations.
My sheep hear My voice, and I know them, and they follow Me.
And I give them eternal life, and they will certainly never perish, and no one will snatch them from My hand.
What My Father has given Me is greater than all, and no one can snatch from the Father’s hand.
I and the Father are one.”
See how the righteous man perished, and no one considers it in his heart. Righteous men are removed, and no one understands. For the righteous man was taken from the presence of injustice.
His burial will be in peace; he has been removed from the midst.
Now I say this, brothers: flesh and blood cannot inherit God’s kingdom, nor does corruption inherit incorruption.
Look, I tell you a mystery: we will not all fall asleep, but we will all be changed,
in an instant, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.
For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.
But when this corruptible puts on incorruption and this mortal puts on immortality, then the written saying will come to pass: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
“Where, death, is your victory? Where, death, is your sting?”
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, knowing that your labor is not empty in the Lord.
and you have forgotten the encouragement that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not make light of the Lord’s discipline, nor faint when reproved by Him.
For the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and scourges every son He receives.”
Endure for discipline. God deals with you as sons; for what son is there whom a father does not discipline?
But if you are without discipline, in which all have become partakers, then you are illegitimate children and not sons.
Furthermore, we had our fathers in the flesh to discipline us, and we respected them. But shall we not much more submit to the Father of spirits and live?
For they disciplined us for a few days according to what seemed right to them, but He for our benefit, so that we may share in His holiness.
Now every discipline seems for the present to be a matter of sorrow, not joy, but afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those trained through it.
As silver and gold are tested in a furnace, so hearts are chosen before the Lord.
The proverbs of Solomon son of David, who reigned in Israel,
for knowing wisdom and discipline and understanding words of good sense,
for receiving turns of speech, understanding true righteousness, and directing judgment rightly,
so that he may give shrewdness to the innocent, perception and thought to a young child.
For a wise person who hears these things will become wiser, and the discerning will acquire guidance,
and understand a comparison and an obscure saying, the utterances of the wise and riddles.

The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom, and good understanding belongs to all who practice it. Reverence toward God is the beginning of perception, but the ungodly will despise wisdom and discipline.
Blessed is the person who found wisdom, the mortal who saw good sense,
for trading in her is better than treasures of gold and silver.
She is more valuable than costly stones; nothing evil will stand against her. She is readily known to all who approach her, and nothing precious is worthy of her.
For length of life and years of living are in her right hand, and wealth and glory in her left.
Righteousness proceeds from her mouth, and she carries law and mercy on her tongue.
Her ways are good ways, and all her paths are in peace.
She is a tree of life to all who hold her fast, and secure for those who lean on her as on the Lord.
God founded the earth by wisdom and prepared the heavens by good sense.
By perception the deeps were split open, and clouds flowed with dew.
From the fruit of righteousness a tree of life grows, but the lives of lawless people are taken away before their time.

“At that hour Michael will pass by, the great angel who stands over the sons of your people. That will be a day of affliction such as has not occurred since they came into being until that day. On that day all the people found inscribed in the book will be exalted.
Many of those sleeping in the breadth of the earth shall arise: some unto everlasting life, others unto reproach, and others unto dispersion and everlasting shame.
Those who understand will appear like heaven’s lights, and those who strengthen my words like the stars of heaven for the age of the age.
The holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom and hold the kingdom for ever, for the age of ages.’

Then I wanted exact understanding of the fourth beast, which destroyed everything and was exceedingly fearsome. Its teeth were iron and its claws bronze, devouring everyone all around and trampling with its feet,
and of its ten horns upon its head and the single other that sprouted, through which three fell out. That horn had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and its appearance surpassed the others.
I observed that horn waging war against the holy ones and routing them,
until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment to the holy ones of the Most High. The time was given, and the holy ones took possession of the kingship.
