I was told concerning the fourth beast that a fourth kingdom would be upon the earth, surpassing the whole earth, overturning it and grinding it down.
As for the kingdom’s ten horns, ten kings will arise, and another king will arise after them. He will surpass the earlier ones in evils and humble three kings.
He will speak words against the Most High, wear down the holy ones of the Most High, and expect to alter seasons and law. Everything will be handed into his hands for a time, times, and half a time.
The judgment will sit; they will destroy the authority and plan to defile and destroy completely.

He gave the kingdom, authority, their greatness, and rule over all the kingdoms under heaven to a holy people of the Most High, to reign with everlasting kingship; all authorities will be subject to him and obey him.
Until the account ended, I, Daniel, was greatly overcome with astonishment; my condition changed, and I fixed the matter in my heart.”

“Rejoice, barren woman who does not give birth! Break out and cry aloud, you who do not labor in childbirth, because the deserted woman’s children are more numerous than those of the woman who has a husband,” for the Lord has spoken.
“Widen the place of your tent and your curtains. Pitch them; do not spare! Lengthen your ropes and strengthen your pegs.
Spread out still farther to right and left. Your offspring will inherit nations, and you will settle deserted cities.
Do not fear because you were put to shame, or be abashed because you were reproached. For you will forget lasting shame and never remember the reproach of your widowhood.
Let no foreigner attached to the Lord say, “Will the Lord then separate me from His people?” And let no eunuch say, “I am a dry tree.”
Thus says the Lord: “To the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths, choose what I wish, and hold fast to My covenant,
I will give them in My house and wall a renowned place better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name, and it will not fail.

And the foreigners attached to the Lord, to serve Him and love the Lord’s name, to become His male and female slaves, and all those keeping My Sabbaths from profanation and holding fast to My covenant—

I will bring them into My holy mountain and make them rejoice in My house of prayer. Their whole burnt offerings and sacrifices will be acceptable on My altar, for My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations,”
And Enoch lived one hundred and sixty-five years, and begot Methuselah.
And Enoch pleased God for two hundred years after he begot Methuselah, and begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enoch were three hundred and sixty-five years.
And Enoch pleased God, and was not found, for God transferred him.
By faith Enoch was taken away so as not to see death, and he was not found, because God took him away. For before his taking away he had received testimony that he had pleased God.
And without faith it is impossible to please Him, for the one approaching God must believe that He is and that He becomes a rewarder of those who seek Him.
Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite replied: “I am younger in time, and you are older; therefore I kept quiet, afraid to announce my own knowledge to you.
I said, ‘Time is what speaks, and in many years people know wisdom.’
But there is a spirit in mortals, and the Almighty’s breath is what teaches.
The long-lived are not wise, nor do elders know judgment.
Therefore I said, ‘Listen to me, and I will announce to you what I know.’
Let no one who is tempted say, “I am being tempted by God.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, and He Himself tempts no one.
But each person is tempted when drawn away and enticed by his own desire.
Then desire, after conceiving, gives birth to sin; and sin, when fully grown, gives birth to death.
Men of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s proclamation; and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.

The queen of the south will be raised at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom; and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.
The conclusion of the matter—the whole is heard: fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole human being.
For God will bring every deed into judgment, concerning everything overlooked, whether good or evil.
Do you not know that all the runners in a stadium run, but one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may obtain it.
Everyone who competes exercises self-control in all things. They do so to receive a perishable wreath, but we an imperishable one.
So I run in this way, not aimlessly; I box in this way, not as one beating the air.
Instead, I pummel my body and bring it into slavery, so that, after proclaiming to others, I myself may not become disqualified.
Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves.
You will recognize them by their fruits. Do people gather grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
In the same way, every good tree bears good fruit, but the rotten tree bears evil fruit.
A good tree cannot bear evil fruit, nor can a rotten tree bear good fruit.
Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.
So then, you will recognize them by their fruits.
for Thou hast upheld my judgment and my cause; Thou sattest on a throne, Thou who judgest righteousness.
Thou didst rebuke nations, and the ungodly one perished; Thou didst erase their name for ever and for the age of the age.
The enemy’s swords failed utterly, and Thou didst pull down cities; their memory perished with a noise.
But by your hardness and unrepentant heart, you store up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and revelation of God’s righteous judgment,
who will repay each according to his works:
to those who, through perseverance in good work, seek glory and honor and incorruptibility, eternal life;
but to those acting from selfish ambition, who disobey the truth but obey unrighteousness, wrath and fury,
affliction and distress upon every human soul that does evil—the Jew first and also the Greek;
but glory and honor and peace to everyone who does good, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
For there is no partiality with God.
Just as the Father loved Me, I also loved you. Remain in My love.
If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love, just as I have kept My Father’s commandments and remain in His love.
An impious person flees when no one pursues, but a righteous person is confident like a lion.

Hear the Lord’s word, you who tremble at His word! Speak, our brothers, to those who hate us and loathe us, so that the Lord’s name may be glorified and seen in their rejoicing; and those people will be ashamed.
Listen, children, to a father’s discipline; pay attention to gain discernment,
for I give you a good gift; do not abandon my law.
For I too became a son obedient to a father and loved in a mother’s presence,
who used to speak to me and teach me: Let our word take hold in your heart;
keep commandments; do not forget or disregard an utterance of my mouth,
and do not abandon her, and she will hold fast to you; love her, and she will keep you.
Fortify her, and she will exalt you; honor her so that she may embrace you,
so that she may give your head a crown of graces and shield you with a crown of delight.
Listen, son, and receive my words, and your years of life will multiply, so that many ways of living may be yours,
for I teach you ways of wisdom and lead you onto straight tracks.
For if you walk, your steps will not be shut in, and if you run, you will not grow weary.
Take hold of my discipline; do not release it, but keep it for yourself for your life.
Do not enter the ways of the ungodly or imitate the ways of the lawless.
Wherever they encamp, do not go there; turn away from them and pass by.
For they will not sleep unless they do harm; their sleep has been taken away, and they do not lie down.
For these people eat food of ungodliness and get drunk on lawless wine.
But the ways of the righteous shine like light; they go forward and illuminate until the day comes right.
But the ways of the ungodly are dark; they do not know how they stumble.
Then He told them a parable: “The land of a certain rich man yielded abundantly.
And he reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to gather my crops?’
And he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will pull down my storehouses and build larger ones, and gather all the grain and my goods there.
And I will say to my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, be glad!”’
But God said to him, ‘Fool, this very night they demand your soul from you; and the things you have prepared—whose will they be?’
So it is with the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.”
For inquire of the former generation; search out the family of the fathers.
For we are of yesterday and do not know; our life on earth is a shadow.
Will these not teach you and tell you, and bring words out of the heart?
Three things are impossible for me to understand, and the fourth I do not comprehend:
the tracks of a flying eagle, and the ways of a snake upon a rock, and the paths of a seagoing ship, and the ways of a man in youth.
For Zion I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem I will not let up until My righteousness goes out like light and My salvation burns like a torch.
Nations will see your righteousness and kings your glory. He will call you your new name, which the Lord will name.
You will be a crown of beauty in the Lord’s hand and a royal diadem in your God’s hand.
He saw, and there was no man; He considered, and there was no one to help. He defended them with His arm and steadied Himself by mercy.
He put on righteousness like a breastplate, placed a helmet of salvation on His head, and wrapped Himself in a garment of vengeance and the cloak,
as one who will repay recompense—reproach to His adversaries.
Those from the west will fear the Lord’s name, and those from sunrise the glorious name. For anger from the Lord will come like a violent river; it will come with wrath.
And He made darkness His hiding place; His tent was around Him, dark water in clouds of the air.
From the far-shining radiance before Him, the clouds passed— hail and coals of fire.
And the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave His voice.
And He sent out arrows and scattered them; He multiplied lightning flashes and threw them into turmoil.
And the springs of the waters appeared, and the foundations of the inhabited world were uncovered at Thy rebuke, Lord, at the blast of the spirit of Thine anger.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and there shall be hail throughout all the land of Egypt, upon men, and upon livestock, and upon every plant upon the earth.”
Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven. The Lord sent thunder and hail, and fire ran over the earth. The Lord rained hail upon all the land of Egypt.
There was hail, with fire flaming amid the hail. The hail was very, very abundant, such as had never been in Egypt since a nation came to be there.
Throughout Egypt the hail struck people and livestock. It struck every plant in the plains and shattered all the trees there.
Only in the land of Goshen, where the sons of Israel were, was there no hail.
He gives rulers nothing to rule and made the earth as nothing.
For they will certainly not sow or plant, nor will their root take hold in the earth. He blew on them, and they dried; a storm will carry them away like brushwood.
“Now then, to whom did you liken Me, and shall I be exalted?” said the Holy One.
Lift your eyes on high and see: Who displayed all these? He brings out His array by number and will call all by name. From abundant glory and in strength’s might, nothing escaped you.
And now, kings, understand; be instructed, all who judge the earth.
Serve the Lord with fear, and exult in Him with trembling.
Take hold of instruction, lest the Lord become angry and you perish from a righteous way. When His fury burns quickly, blessed are all who have trusted in Him.
Let every soul submit to the higher authorities, for there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been appointed by God.
Therefore the one who sets himself against authority has resisted God’s ordering, and those who resist will receive judgment upon themselves.
For rulers are not a terror to good work, but to evil. Do you want to be free from fear of the authority? Do the good, and you will have praise from it;

for it is God’s servant to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid; for it does not bear the sword without purpose. For it is God’s servant, an avenger who brings wrath on the one who practices evil.
That slave who knew his master’s will and did not prepare or act according to his will shall receive many blows.

But the one who did not know and did things deserving blows shall receive few. From everyone to whom much was given, much will be required; and from the one to whom they entrusted much, they will ask all the more.
Look at the One who hates lawless things and destroys the wicked, who is eternally righteous.
Ungodly is the one saying to a king, ‘You act lawlessly,’ and to rulers, ‘Most ungodly one,’
who did not stand in awe before an honored person, nor knows how to give honor to powerful men so as to admire their persons.
You will proclaim wisdom, so that understanding may heed you.
For she is on the high summits, and stands between the paths.
For she sits beside the gates of rulers, and is praised at the entrances:
“You, O human beings, I summon, and I send forth my voice to the children of humankind.
Understand resourcefulness, you innocent ones; and you uneducated, put your heart into it.
Listen to me, for I will speak noble things, and bring forth upright things from my lips.
For my throat will meditate on truth, and lying lips are detestable before me.
All the words of my mouth are with righteousness; there is nothing crooked or entangled in them.
They are all plain to those who understand, and upright to those who find knowledge.
Take discipline rather than silver, and knowledge above tested gold; choose discernment rather than pure gold.
For wisdom is better than costly stones, and nothing precious is worthy of her.
I, Wisdom, have made counsel my dwelling, and I have called upon knowledge and reflection.
The fear of the Lord hates injustice, insolence and arrogance and the ways of wicked people; and I hate the perverted ways of evil people.
Counsel and security are mine; understanding is mine, and strength is mine.
Through me kings reign, and rulers write righteousness.
Through me great men become great, and through me sovereigns rule the earth.
I love those who love me, and those who seek me will find me.
Wealth and glory belong to me, and possession of many things and righteousness.
It is better to reap me than gold and precious stone, and my produce is better than choice silver.
I walk in ways of righteousness, and move in the midst of paths of just judgment,
so that I may apportion substance to those who love me, and fill their storehouses with good things.
If I announce to you the things that happen day by day, I will remember to recount the things from eternity.
The Lord created me as the beginning of His ways, for His works.
Before the age He founded me, in the beginning,
before making the earth and before making the deeps, before the springs of the waters came forth,
before the mountains were established, and before all hills He gives me birth.
The Lord made countries and uninhabited places, and the inhabited extremities of the world beneath heaven.
When He was preparing heaven, I was present with Him, and when He was marking out His own throne upon winds.
When He was making the clouds above strong, and when He was setting the springs of the world beneath heaven secure,
and was making the foundations of the earth strong,
I was beside Him, fitting things together; I was the one in whom He delighted. Day by day I rejoiced before Him at every time,
when He rejoiced after completing the inhabited world, and delighted in the children of humankind.
Now, therefore, son, listen to me.
Happy is the man who will listen to me, and the person who will keep my ways, staying awake at my doors day by day, guarding the posts of my entrances.
For my ways out are ways out to life, and favor is prepared by the Lord.
But those who sin against me act impiously against their own lives, and those who hate me love death.”
Wisdom is celebrated at the exits, and in the squares she speaks openly.
At the tops of walls she is proclaimed; at rulers’ gates she sits nearby, and at city gates she speaks boldly:
As long as the innocent hold to righteousness, they will not be ashamed. But the senseless, desiring insolence, became ungodly and hated perception,
and became liable to reproofs. Behold, I will send forth to you an utterance of my breath, and I will teach you my word.
Son, do not drift away; keep my counsel and thought,
so that your soul may live and grace be around your neck.
There will be healing for your flesh and care for your bones,
so that you may walk all your ways confidently in peace, and your foot will certainly not stumble.
For if you sit, you will be fearless, and if you sleep, you will sleep pleasantly.
You will not fear an approaching fright or the oncoming assaults of the ungodly,
for the Lord will be upon all your ways and support your foot so that you are not shaken.
“If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.
And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate, so that He may be with you forever:
the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither beholds Him nor knows Him. You know Him, because He remains with you and will be in you.
One who does evil is an abomination to a king, for a throne of rule is prepared with righteousness.
Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show his works by good conduct in the gentleness of wisdom.
But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, do not boast against the truth and lie against it.
This is not the wisdom coming down from above; it is earthly, merely natural, demonic.
For where there are jealousy and selfish ambition, there are disorder and every foul practice.
But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, considerate, open to persuasion, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial, without hypocrisy.
And a fruit of righteousness is sown in peace for those who make peace.
Those who have no steering fall like leaves, but deliverance is in much counsel.
There was a small city with few people in it; a great king might come against it, surround it and build great siegeworks against it,
and he might find in it a poor wise man, who will deliver the city by his wisdom; yet no one remembered that poor man.
I said, Wisdom is better than strength; yet the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
The words of the wise, heard quietly, are better than the shouting of rulers in follies.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner will destroy much good.
And God formed man from the dust of the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
Then Job rose, tore his garments, and cut off the hair of his head. He fell to the ground, bowed in worship, and said:
“I myself came out naked from my mother’s womb, and naked I shall depart there: the Lord gave, and the Lord took away; as it seemed good to the Lord, so it happened: blessed be the name of the Lord.”
In all these things that happened to him, Job did not sin at all before the Lord or attribute foolishness to God.
While they were there, the time came for her to give birth.
She bore her firstborn Son, wrapped Him in swaddling cloths, and laid Him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the lodging place.
In that same region there were shepherds living in the fields and keeping watch over their flock through the watches of the night.
An angel of the Lord stood beside them, and the Lord’s glory shone around them; they feared with a great fear.
The angel said to them, “Do not fear, for behold, I announce to you good news of great joy, which will be for all the people:
today in David’s city a Savior has been born for you, who is Christ the Lord.
This is the sign for you: you will find an infant wrapped in swaddling cloths and lying in a manger.”
But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives to all generously and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
But let him ask in faith, doubting nothing, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.
For that person must not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord,
a man of divided mind, unstable in all his ways.
You are My friends if you do what I command you.
I no longer call you slaves, because the slave does not know what his master is doing; but I have called you friends, because I have made known to you everything that I heard from My Father.

And Moses said to the Lord, “I beseech Thee, Lord, I have not been capable—not yesterday, nor the day before, nor since Thou didst begin to speak to Thy servant; for I am weak of voice and slow of tongue.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Who gave a human being a mouth? Who made one hard of hearing or deaf, seeing or blind? Is it not I, God?
Now therefore go, and I will open your mouth, and teach you what you are to speak.”
For I set all this upon my heart, and my heart saw all this: the righteous, the wise and their works are in God’s hand. A person knows neither love nor hatred; everything lies before them.
For Thou didst acquire my kidneys, Lord; Thou didst support me from my mother’s womb.
I will thank Thee, for I was made fearfully wonderful; wondrous are Thy works, and my soul knows very well.
My bone was not hidden from Thee, which Thou madest in secret, and my substance in earth’s lowest places.
Thine eyes saw my unworked substance, and in Thy book all will be written; they will be formed over days, and none among them.
And God said, “Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven to give light upon the earth and to divide the day from the night. Let them serve for signs and seasons, for days and years.
And let them be lights in the firmament of heaven, to shine upon the earth.” And it was so.
And God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night; He made the stars also.
And God set them in the firmament of heaven to shine upon the earth,
to rule the day and the night, and to divide the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
The Lord appeared to Solomon in sleep at night. The Lord said to Solomon, “Ask a request for yourself.”

Solomon said, “Thou showedst great mercy to Thy servant David my father, as he walked before Thee in truth, righteousness, and uprightness of heart with Thee. Thou keptest this great mercy for him, placing his son on his throne, as it is this day.
Now, Lord my God, Thou hast placed Thy servant in place of my father David. I am a little child and do not know my going out or my coming in.
Thy servant is among Thy people whom Thou didst choose, a numerous people who cannot be numbered.
Give Thy servant a heart to hear and to judge Thy people in righteousness, discerning between good and evil; for who can judge this weighty people of Thine?”
It pleased the Lord that Solomon had asked this.
The Lord said to him, “Because you have asked this of Me and have not asked for many days for yourself, or wealth, or the lives of your enemies, but have asked for understanding to hear judgment,
behold, I have done according to your word. Behold, I have given you a discerning and wise heart, so that no one like you has been before you, and no one like you shall arise after you.
I have also given you what you did not ask: both wealth and glory, so that no man like you has been among the kings.
If you walk in My way, keeping My commandments and ordinances as your father David walked, I will multiply your days.”

The appointed officers thus provided for King Solomon and all the orders for the king’s table, each in his month; they did not depart from an instruction. They brought barley and straw for the horses and chariots to the place where the king would be, each according to his assignment.
These were Solomon’s requirements for one day: thirty kors of fine flour and sixty kors of pounded meal,
ten choice calves, twenty pasture-fed cattle, and a hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, and choice birds—fattened provisions.
For he was ruler beyond the River, and he had peace on every side around him.
The Lord gave Solomon discernment, very great wisdom, and abundance of heart like the sand beside the sea.
Solomon increased greatly beyond the discernment of all ancient people and beyond all the discerning people of Egypt.
He became wiser than all people; he became wiser than Gaithan the Ezraite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mal.
Solomon spoke three thousand parables, and his songs numbered five thousand.
He spoke about trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing through the wall. He spoke about livestock, birds, creeping things, and fish.
All the peoples came to hear Solomon’s wisdom, and he received gifts from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.
In many portions and in many ways, God spoke long ago to the fathers in the prophets,
but in these last days He spoke to us in a Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, through whom He also made the ages.
He is the radiance of His glory and the imprint of His being, upholding all things by the word of His power. Having made purification of sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high,
having become so much greater than the angels as the name He has inherited is more excellent than theirs.
How great Thy works have become, Lord! Thou madest all things in wisdom; the earth was filled with Thy possession.
Here is the sea, great and spacious; there are creeping things without number, living creatures small with great.
There ships pass, and this dragon, which Thou didst form to play with it.
All wait for Thee to give them food at the right time.
When Thou givest to them, they will gather; when Thou openest Thy hand, all things will be filled with goodness.
When Thou turnest Thy face away, they will be troubled. Thou wilt take back their breath, and they will fail and return to their dust.
Thou wilt send Thy Spirit, and they will be created, and Thou wilt renew the face of the earth.

because in Him all things were created, in the heavens and upon the earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities. All things have been created through Him and for Him.
And He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.
But where was wisdom found, and what is the place of understanding?
It has escaped every human and was hidden from the birds of heaven.
Destruction and Death said, ‘We have heard its renown.’
God established its way well, and He knows its place.
For He observes the whole realm under heaven, knowing everything in the earth that He made:
the weight of winds and measures of water;
when He acted in this way, He counted rain and a path for sounds amid a shaking.
Then He saw wisdom and expounded it; having prepared it, He traced it out.
And He said to a human, ‘Behold, reverence for God is wisdom, and abstaining from evils is knowledge.’”
when I went out early in the city, and my chair was set in the squares.
Young men saw me and hid, and all the elders stood.
Powerful men stopped speaking, placing a finger upon their mouths.
Those who heard called me blessed, and their tongues clung to their throats.
For an ear heard and called me blessed, and an eye that saw me turned aside.
Then two women who were prostitutes appeared before the king and stood before him.
One woman said, “Please, my lord, this woman and I live in one house, and we gave birth in the house.
On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth. We were together, with no one in the house except the two of us.
This woman’s son died during the night when she lay on him.
She rose in the middle of the night and took my son from my arms. She laid him in her bosom, and laid her dead son in my bosom.
I rose in the morning to nurse my son, and that child was dead. I looked carefully at him in the morning, and he was not my son whom I had borne.”
The other woman said, “No! My son is the living one, and your son is the dead one.” Thus they spoke before the king.
The king said to them, “You say, ‘This is my son, the living one, and her son is the dead one.’ And you say, ‘No! My son is the living one, and your son is the dead one.’”
The king said, “Bring me a sword.” They brought the sword before the king.
The king said, “Divide the living nursing child in two. Give half of it to this woman and half of it to this woman.”

The woman whose son was alive answered the king, for her womb was stirred for her son. She said, “Please, my lord, give her the child! You must not put him to death!” But the other said, “He shall belong to neither me nor her. Divide him.”
The king answered, “Give the child to the woman who said, ‘Give it to her,’ and you must not put him to death. She is his mother.”
All Israel heard this judgment the king had given, and they feared the king, for they saw that God’s discernment was within him to carry out justice.

The Lord, the God of Israel, chose me from all my father’s house to be king over Israel for ever. He chose the royal power in Judah, and from Judah’s house my father’s house, and among my father’s sons He was willing that I become king over all Israel.
From all my sons—for the Lord gave me many sons—He chose Solomon my son to seat him upon the throne of the Lord’s kingdom over Israel.
God said to me, ‘Solomon your son will build My house and My court, for I have chosen him to be My son, and I will be a Father to him,
and I will set his kingdom upright for ever, if he remains strong to observe My commandments and My judgments, as on this day.’

Now, before the whole assembly of the Lord and in the ears of our God, observe and seek all the commandments of the Lord our God, so that you may inherit the good land and pass it on as an inheritance to your sons after you for ever.

And now, Solomon my son, know the God of your fathers, and serve Him with a whole heart and a willing soul; for the Lord examines every heart and knows every thought. If you seek Him, He shall be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you utterly.
See, therefore, that the Lord has chosen you to build Him a house as a sanctuary. Be strong and act.”
O Lord, I am Thy slave; I am Thy slave and the son of Thy slave woman. Thou hast torn apart my bonds.
Who measured the water with His hand, heaven with a span, and all the earth with a handful? Who weighed mountains with a weight and wooded valleys with a balance?
Who knew the Lord’s mind, and who became His counselor to instruct Him?
With whom did He take counsel, and who instructed Him? Who showed Him judgment, or who showed Him the way of understanding?
For we know that if our earthly house, this tent, is dismantled, we have a building from God, a house not made by hands, eternal in the heavens.
For indeed in this we groan, longing to be clothed over with our dwelling from heaven,
if indeed, even after being unclothed, we shall not be found naked.
For indeed we who are in the tent groan, being burdened, because we do not wish to be unclothed but to be clothed over, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
If I told you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?
And no one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven, the Son of Man.
The one who has My commandments and keeps them is the one who loves Me. And the one who loves Me will be loved by My Father, and I will love him and reveal Myself to him.”
Judas—not the Iscariot—says to Him, “Lord, what then has happened that Thou art going to reveal Thyself to us and not to the world?”
Jesus answered and said to him, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word, and My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our dwelling with him.
The one who does not love Me does not keep My words. And the word that you hear is not Mine, but the Father’s who sent Me.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
He was in the beginning with God.
All things came into being through Him, and without Him not one thing came into being. What has come into being
in Him was life, and the life was the light of humankind.
And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.
Say that wisdom is your sister, and acquire understanding as your familiar companion,
so that she may keep you from an alien and wicked woman, if she catches you with pleasing words.
Kind is the man who has compassion and lends; he will manage his words with judgment.
For he will never be shaken; the righteous person will be an everlasting memorial.
By the Lord’s word the heavens were established, and by the spirit of His mouth all their power.
He gathers the sea’s waters like a wineskin; He places the deeps in storehouses.
Let all the earth fear the Lord; let all who inhabit the world be shaken before Him.
For He spoke, and they came to be; He commanded, and they were created.
For Solomon. God, give Thy judgment to the king, and Thy righteousness to the king’s son,
to judge Thy people in righteousness, and Thy poor in justice.
Let the mountains take up peace for Thy people, and the hills in righteousness.
He will judge the poor of the people, and save the children of the needy, and humble the false accuser,
Where is the wise person? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Has not God made the world’s wisdom foolish?
For since, in God’s wisdom, the world did not know God through wisdom, God was pleased through the foolishness of the proclamation to save those who believe.
For Jews ask for signs and Greeks seek wisdom,
but we proclaim Christ crucified: a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,
but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is God’s power and God’s wisdom.
For God’s foolishness is wiser than human beings, and God’s weakness is stronger than human beings.
Yet we speak wisdom among the mature, a wisdom belonging neither to this age nor to the rulers of this age, who are being brought to nothing.
Instead, we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery, the hidden wisdom that God appointed beforehand, before the ages, for our glory.
None of the rulers of this age has known it; for if they had known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
But as it is written, “What an eye has not seen and an ear has not heard, and what has not arisen in a human heart—these are the things God prepared for those who love Him.”
But God revealed them to us through the Spirit, for the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.
For who among human beings knows the things of a person except the person’s spirit within? So also no one has known the things of God except the Spirit of God.
Now we did not receive the spirit of the world but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may know the things freely given to us by God.
We also speak these things, not in words taught by human wisdom but in those taught by the Spirit, explaining spiritual things to spiritual people.
But a natural person does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to such a person, who cannot know them because they are discerned spiritually.
The spiritual person discerns all things, but is himself discerned by no one.
For “Who has known the Lord’s mind, so as to instruct Him?” But we have Christ’s mind.
For if wisdom enters your mind and perception seems good to your soul,
good counsel will guard you, and holy thought will keep you,
so that it may rescue you from an evil way and from a man who says nothing trustworthy.
And after some time Cain brought an offering to the Lord from the fruits of the earth.
And Abel also brought an offering from the firstborn of his sheep and from their fat. And God looked with favour upon Abel and his gifts,
but He gave no heed to Cain and his offerings. And Cain was greatly distressed, and his face fell.
And the Lord God said to Cain, “Why are you so distressed, and why has your face fallen?
If you offer rightly but do not divide rightly, have you not sinned? Be still. His turning shall be toward you, and you shall rule over him.”
And Cain said to Abel his brother, “Let us go out into the field.” And while they were in the field, Cain rose against Abel his brother and slew him.
And God said to Cain, “Where is Abel your brother?” And he said, “I do not know. Am I my brother’s keeper?”
And God said, “What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries unto Me from the earth.
And now you are cursed from the earth, which opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
When you till the earth, it shall no longer yield its strength to you. You shall be groaning and trembling upon the earth.”
And Cain said to the Lord, “My guilt is too great for me to be forgiven.
If Thou dost cast me out this day from the face of the earth, I shall be hidden from Thy face; and I shall be groaning and trembling upon the earth, and whoever finds me shall slay me.”
And the Lord God said to him, “Not so. Whoever slays Cain shall incur sevenfold vengeance.” And the Lord God set a mark upon Cain, that no one finding him should slay him.
And Cain went out from the face of God and dwelt in the land of Nod, opposite Eden.
And the Lord God saw that the wickedness of mankind had multiplied upon the earth, and that each one continually set his heart upon evil all his days.
And God took to heart that He had made man upon the earth, and pondered it.
And God said, “I will blot out from the face of the earth the mankind I have made, together with the cattle, the creeping things, and the birds of heaven; for I am angered that I made them.”
But Noah found grace before the Lord God.
These are the generations of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation; Noah pleased God.
And God said to Noah, “The time of all mankind has come before Me, for the earth is filled with unrighteousness because of them; and behold, I am destroying them and the earth.
“Therefore make yourself an ark of squared timber. Make compartments within the ark, and coat it inside and out with pitch.
And this is how you shall make it: the ark shall be three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
Make the ark taper toward the top, and finish it to a cubit above. Set the door of the ark in its side, and make it with lower, second, and third storeys.
“And behold, I am bringing a flood of water upon the earth, to destroy all flesh beneath heaven in which is the breath of life. Everything upon the earth shall die.
But I will establish My covenant with you. And you shall enter the ark, you and your sons, your wife and your sons’ wives with you.
“And from all the cattle, all the creeping things, all the wild beasts, and all flesh, you shall bring two of each into the ark, to sustain them with you. They shall be male and female.

Of all the winged birds according to their kind, all the cattle according to their kind, and all the creeping things upon the earth according to their kinds, two of each shall come to you, male and female, to be sustained with you.
“And take for yourself every kind of food that is eaten, and gather it to yourself. It shall be food for you and for them.”
And Noah did all that the Lord God commanded him; so he did.
And the flood was upon the earth for forty days and forty nights. And the waters increased and lifted the ark, and it rose above the earth.
And the waters prevailed and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark floated upon the waters.
And the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth, and covered all the high mountains beneath heaven.
The waters rose fifteen cubits above them and covered all the high mountains.
And all flesh that moved upon the earth died: birds, cattle, wild beasts, every creeping thing that moves upon the earth, and all mankind.
Everything that had the breath of life, everything upon the dry land, died.

And He blotted out every living thing upon the face of the whole earth: mankind, cattle, creeping things, and the birds of heaven. They were blotted out from the earth, and only Noah remained, and those with him in the ark.
And the whole earth had one language, and all shared one speech.
And as they journeyed from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
And each said to his neighbour, “Come, let us make bricks and burn them in the fire.” And they used brick for stone, and pitch for mortar.
And they said, “Come, let us build ourselves a city and a tower whose summit shall reach unto heaven, and let us make a name for ourselves before we are scattered over the face of the whole earth.”
And the Lord came down to see the city and the tower which the children of men had built.
And the Lord said, “Behold, they are one people, and all have one language; and this they have begun to do. And now nothing that they purpose to do shall fail them.
“Come, let Us go down and confound their language there, so that they may no longer understand one another’s speech.”
And the Lord scattered them from there over the face of the whole earth, and they ceased building the city and the tower.
Therefore its name was called Confusion, because there the Lord confounded the languages of the whole earth, and from there the Lord God scattered them over the face of the whole earth.
And after these things God tested Abraham, and said to him, “Abraham, Abraham.” And he said, “Behold, here am I.”
And He said, “Take your son, your beloved, whom you have loved, Isaac, and go to the high land; and offer him there for a whole burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I shall tell you.”

And Abraham rose in the morning, and saddled his female donkey, and took with him two servants and Isaac his son. And he split wood for the whole burnt offering, and arose and went, and came to the place of which God had spoken to him.
On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place far off.
And Abraham said to his servants, “Stay here with the female donkey; and I and the lad will go over there, and worship, and return to you.”
And Abraham took the wood of the whole burnt offering, and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he took the fire in his hand, and the knife. And the two went together.
And Isaac spoke to Abraham his father, and said, “Father.” And he said, “What is it, child?” And he said, “Behold the fire and the wood; but where is the sheep for the whole burnt offering?”
And Abraham said, “God will provide for Himself a sheep for the whole burnt offering, child.” And the two went together,

and came to the place of which God had spoken to him. And Abraham built an altar there, and laid the wood upon it, and bound together the feet of Isaac his son, and laid him upon the altar, upon the wood.
And Abraham stretched out his hand to take the knife, to slaughter his son.
And an angel of the Lord called to him out of the heaven, and said to him, “Abraham, Abraham.” And he said, “Behold, here am I.”
And he said, “Do not lay your hand upon the lad or do anything to him; for now I know that you fear God, and have not spared your beloved son for my sake.”

And Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, one ram was caught by its horns in a sabek plant. And Abraham went and took the ram, and offered it for a whole burnt offering instead of Isaac his son.
And at dawn, the angels urged Lot, saying, “Arise, take your wife and your two daughters whom you have, and depart, so that you do not perish with the lawless deeds of the city.”
And they were troubled; and the angels took hold of his hand, and the hand of his wife, and the hands of his two daughters, because the Lord spared him.

And when they had brought them outside, they said, “Save your own life. Do not look behind you or stand anywhere in the surrounding country. Escape to the mountain, so that you are not swept away with them.”
And Lot said to them, “I beg you, lord,
for your servant has found mercy before you, and you have shown me your great righteousness by preserving my life. Yet I cannot escape to the mountain, for calamities may overtake me, and I may die.
Behold, this city is near enough for me to flee to, and it is small. There I shall be saved; is it not small? And my soul shall live.”
And he said to him, “Behold, I have regarded your face in this matter also, that I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken.
So hurry and be saved there; for I can do nothing until you enter it.” Therefore he called the name of that city Zoar.
The sun rose upon the earth, and Lot entered into Zoar.
And the Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah sulphur and fire from the Lord out of the heaven;
and He overthrew those cities, and all the surrounding country, and all that lived in the cities, and all that sprang from the earth.
And his wife looked behind her, and became a pillar of salt.
And Abraham rose early in the morning, and went to the place where he had stood before the Lord.
And he looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and toward the land of the surrounding country; and he saw, and behold, a flame rose from the earth as the vapour of a furnace.
And when the Lord blotted out all the cities of the surrounding country, God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out from the midst of the overthrow, when the Lord overthrew the cities where Lot lived.

And Esau bore a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him; and Esau said in his mind, “Let the days of mourning for my father draw near, that I may kill Jacob my brother.”
And the words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah; and she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said to him, “Behold, Esau your brother threatens to kill you.
“Now therefore, my child, obey my voice, and arise and flee into Mesopotamia, to Laban my brother at Harran.
“And stay with him a few days, until the fury
“and anger of your brother turn away from you, and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send and bring you back from there, lest I be bereaved of you both in one day.”
And Jacob went out from the Well of the Oath, and went toward Harran.
And he came upon a place and slept there, for the sun had set; and he took one of the stones of the place, and put it by his head, and slept in that place.
And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder was set upon the earth, whose top reached to heaven; and the angels of God ascended and descended upon it.
And the Lord stood firm upon it, and said, “I am the Lord, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac. Do not fear; the land on which you sleep I will give to you and to your seed.

“And your seed shall be as the sand of the earth, and shall spread toward the sea, and toward the south, and toward the north, and toward the east; and in you and in your seed all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed.
“And behold, I am with you, guarding you on every road wherever you go; and I will bring you back into this land, for I will not forsake you until I have done all that I have spoken to you.”
And Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, “The Lord is in this place, and I did not know it.”
And he was afraid and said, “How fearful is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.”
And Jacob rose in the morning, and took the stone which he had put there by his head, and set it up as a pillar, and poured oil upon its top.
And Jacob called the name of that place House of God; but the name of the city at first was Oulamlous.
And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, “If the Lord God is with me, and guards me on this way that I go, and gives me bread to eat and clothing to wear,
“and brings me back in safety to my father’s house, then the Lord shall be my God.
“And this stone, which I have set up as a pillar, shall be to me a house of God; and of all that Thou givest me I will surely give a tenth to Thee.”
“And you yourselves know that with all my strength I have served your father.
“And your father has cheated me, and changed my wages of ten lambs; but God has not allowed him to harm me.
“If he said, ‘The variously marked shall be your wages,’ then all the sheep bore variously marked young; and if he said, ‘The white shall be your wages,’ then all the sheep bore white young.
“And God has taken away all your father’s livestock, and given them to me.
“And when the sheep were mating, I saw them with my eyes in a dream; and behold, the male goats and rams mounting the sheep and goats were white-marked, variously marked, and ash-grey with spots.
“And the angel of God said to me in a dream, ‘Jacob.’ And I said, ‘What is it?’
“And he said, ‘Lift up your eyes and see the male goats and rams mounting the sheep and goats, white-marked, variously marked, and ash-grey with spots; for I have seen all that Laban does to you.

“‘I am the God who appeared to you in the place of God, where you anointed a pillar to Me, and vowed a vow to Me. Now therefore arise and go out from this land, and depart to the land of your birth, and I will be with you.’”
And God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream by night, and said to him, “Take care not to speak evil to Jacob.”
And Laban overtook Jacob. And Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain; and Laban stationed his kinsmen in the mountain of Gilead.
And Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done? Why did you flee secretly, and defraud me, and lead away my daughters as captives of the sword?
“If you had told me, I would have sent you away with gladness and music, with tambourines and lyre.
“I was not deemed worthy to kiss my children and my daughters. Now you have acted foolishly.
“And now my hand has power to harm you; but the God of your father said to me yesterday, ‘Take care not to speak evil to Jacob.’
“These twenty years I have been with you; your sheep and your goats have not miscarried, and I have not eaten the rams of your flock.
“I brought you no animal taken by wild beasts; I myself paid for what was stolen by day and what was stolen by night.
“By day I was consumed by the heat, and by night by the frost; and sleep departed from my eyes.
“These twenty years I have been in your house; I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years among your sheep; and you defrauded me of my wages of ten ewe lambs.
“Unless the God of my father Abraham and the Fear of Isaac had been with me, you would now have sent me away empty. God saw my humiliation and the toil of my hands, and rebuked you yesterday.”
And he rose that night, and took his two wives and his two slave women and his eleven children, and crossed the ford of Jabbok.
And he took them and crossed the torrent, and brought over all that he had.
And Jacob was left alone; and a man wrestled with him until morning.
And he saw that he could not prevail against him, and touched the broad part of his thigh; and the broad part of Jacob’s thigh became numb as he wrestled with him.
And he said to him, “Let me go, for dawn has risen.” And he said, “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”
And he said to him, “What is your name?” And he said, “Jacob.”
And he said to him, “Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name, for you have been strong with God, and with men you are mighty.”
And Jacob asked and said, “Tell me your name.” And he said, “Why do you ask my name?” And he blessed him there.
And Jacob called the name of that place Form of God, “For I have seen God face to face, and my life has been preserved.”
And the sun rose upon him as he passed Form of God; and he limped because of his thigh.
And when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of the tunic of many colours which was upon him.
And they took him and cast him into the pit; and the pit was empty, having no water.

And they sat down to eat bread; and they lifted up their eyes and saw, and behold, Ishmaelite travellers were coming from Gilead, and their camels were laden with spices and resin and stacte; and they were going to take them down into Egypt.
And Judah said to his brothers, “What profit is there if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?
“Come, let us sell him to these Ishmaelites, and do not let our hands be upon him, for he is our brother and our flesh.” And his brothers listened.
And Midianite merchants passed by; and they drew Joseph up and brought him out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of gold, and brought Joseph down into Egypt.
And after these things his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph, and said, “Lie with me.”
But he would not, and said to his master’s wife, “If my master concerns himself with nothing in his house because of me, and has committed all that he has into my hands,
“and nothing in this house is above me, and nothing has been withheld from me except you, because you are his wife, how shall I do this evil thing, and sin before God?”
And though she spoke to Joseph day after day, he did not listen to her, to sleep with her and have relations with her.
And on a certain day Joseph entered the house to do his work, and none of the household was inside.
And she caught him by his garments, saying, “Lie with me.” And he left his garments in her hands, and fled and went outside.
And when she saw that he had left his garments in her hands, and had fled and gone outside,
she called those of the household, and said to them, “See, he has brought us a Hebrew servant to mock us. He came in to me, saying, ‘Lie with me’; and I cried with a loud voice.
“And when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garments beside me, and fled and went outside.”
And she kept his garments beside her until his master came to his house.
And she spoke to him in this way, saying, “The Hebrew servant whom you have brought to us came in to me to mock me, and said to me, ‘I will lie with you.’
“And when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garments beside me, and fled and went outside.”
And when his master heard the words of his wife which she spoke to him, saying, “This is what your servant did to me,” his anger was kindled.
And Joseph’s master took him and cast him into the fortress, into the place where the king’s prisoners were held in the fortress.
And the Lord was with Joseph, and poured mercy upon him, and gave him grace before the chief jailer.
And the chief jailer committed the prison into Joseph’s hand, and all those confined in the prison, and all that they did there.
And the chief jailer concerned himself with nothing because of him; for all was in Joseph’s hand, because the Lord was with him, and whatever he did, the Lord made it prosper in his hands.
And the words pleased Pharaoh and all his servants.
And Pharaoh said to all his servants, “Shall we find such a man as this, who has the Spirit of God in him?”
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has shown you all these things, there is no man more prudent and discerning than you.
“You shall be over my house, and all my people shall obey your mouth; only in the throne shall I be above you.”
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Behold, I set you today over all the land of Egypt.”
And Pharaoh took his ring from his hand and put it upon Joseph’s hand, and clothed him in a robe of fine linen, and put a golden collar about his neck.
And he made him ride in his second chariot, and a herald proclaimed before him; and he set him over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh; without you no one shall lift up his hand in all the land of Egypt.”
And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Psonthomphanech; and he gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, to be his wife.
For if God did not spare angels when they sinned, but cast them into Tartarus and handed them over to chains of gloom, kept for judgment,
and did not spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah, a herald of righteousness, as one of eight, when He brought a flood upon a world of ungodly people,
and reduced the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes, condemning them to overthrow, having made them an example for those who would live ungodly lives,
and rescued righteous Lot, who was distressed by the lawless people’s conduct in debauchery—
for by what he saw and heard, that righteous man, living among them, tormented his righteous soul day after day over their lawless deeds—
then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment,
Go, say to the sons of Israel: ‘I am the Lord. I will bring you out from the Egyptians’ domination and deliver you from slavery. I will ransom you with an uplifted arm and with great judgment.
And I will take you to Myself for a people, and I will be your God; and you shall know that I am the Lord your God, who brought you out from the oppression of the Egyptians.
I will bring you into the land concerning which I stretched out My hand to give it to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will give it to you as an inheritance. I am the Lord.’”
And the Lord said to Moses, “Behold, I have made you a god to Pharaoh; and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet.
You shall speak to him all that I command you; and Aaron your brother shall speak to Pharaoh, that he may let the sons of Israel go out of his land.
I will harden Pharaoh’s heart and multiply My signs and My wonders in the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh will not listen to you. I will lay My hand on Egypt and bring out My people, the sons of Israel, from the land of Egypt with My power and great vengeance.
All the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord when I stretch out My hand over Egypt and bring the sons of Israel out from among them.”
Moses and Aaron did as the Lord commanded them; so they did.
God led them by day in a pillar of cloud to show them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire.
The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not cease before all the people.
Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. The Lord drove the sea back with a violent south wind all night and made the sea dry. The water was split.
The sons of Israel entered the midst of the sea on dry ground, and the water was a wall for them on the right and a wall on the left.
The Egyptians pursued them, and all Pharaoh’s horses, the chariots, and the riders entered after them into the midst of the sea.
During the morning watch, the Lord looked on the Egyptians’ camp in a pillar of fire and cloud and threw the Egyptians’ camp into confusion.
He bound the axles of their chariots and drove them with force. The Egyptians said, “Let us flee from Israel, for the Lord is fighting for them against the Egyptians.”
And the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea, and let the water return and cover the Egyptians, both their chariots and their riders.”
Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and toward daybreak the water returned to its place. The Egyptians fled beneath the water, and the Lord shook the Egyptians into the midst of the sea.
The water returned and covered the chariots, the riders, and all Pharaoh’s force that had entered the sea after them. Not one of them remained.
But the sons of Israel walked on dry ground in the midst of the sea, and the water was a wall for them on the right and a wall on the left.
The Lord rescued Israel that day from the Egyptians’ hand, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore.
Israel saw the great hand in what the Lord had done to the Egyptians. The people feared the Lord and trusted God and His attendant Moses.
Then Moses and the sons of Israel sang this song to God, saying: “Let us sing to the Lord, for He has been gloriously glorified; horse and rider He has cast into the sea.
He has become a helper and a shelter to me for salvation; He is my God, and I will glorify Him; the God of my father, and I will exalt Him.
The Lord shatters wars; the Lord is His name.
Pharaoh’s chariots and his host He has cast into the sea; chosen riders, officers, He has drowned in the Red Sea.
With the sea He covered them; they sank into the deep as a stone.
Thy right hand, O Lord, has been glorified in strength; Thy right hand, O Lord, has shattered enemies.
Lord our Lord, how wondrous is Thy name in all the earth, for Thy magnificence was raised above the heavens.
From the mouth of infants and nursing children Thou didst prepare praise, because of Thine enemies, to bring down the enemy and the avenger.
For I will see the heavens, works of Thy fingers, the moon and stars which Thou didst found:
Jacob withdrew to Syria’s plain; Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept guard.
Through a prophet the Lord brought Israel up from Egypt, and through a prophet he was preserved.
Ephraim provoked anger and exasperation; his blood will be poured upon him, and the Lord will repay him for his reproach.
All the commandments which I command you this day you shall take heed to do, that you may live and multiply, and enter and inherit the land which the Lord your God sware unto your fathers.

And you shall remember all the way wherein the Lord your God led you in the wilderness, to afflict you and to test you, that the things in your heart might be known, whether you would keep His commandments or not.

And He afflicted you, and made you hunger, and fed you with manna, which your fathers did not know, that He might declare unto you that man shall not live by bread alone, but man shall live by every word that proceeds through the mouth of God.
Your garments did not wear out upon you, neither did your feet become calloused; behold, these forty years.
And you shall know in your heart that, as a man chastens his son, so shall the Lord your God chasten you.
you become lifted up in heart, and forget the Lord your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage;

who led you through that great and fearful wilderness, wherein were biting serpents, and scorpions, and thirst, where there was no water; who brought forth for you a spring of water out of the sheer rock;
who fed you with manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know, to afflict you and to test you, and to do you good in your latter days.
The whole congregation of the sons of Israel set out from the wilderness of Sin by their encampments, at the Lord’s word, and camped at Rephidim. There was no water for the people to drink.
And the people reviled Moses, saying, “Give us water, that we may drink.” And Moses said to them, “Why do you revile me? And why do you test the Lord?”
And the people thirsted there for water, and murmured against Moses, saying, “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our livestock with thirst?”
Moses cried out to the Lord, “What shall I do with this people? A little more, and they will stone me to death!”
And the Lord said to Moses, “Go before this people, and take with you some of the elders of the people; and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the river, and go.
Behold, I stand before you there upon the rock in Horeb; and you shall strike the rock, and water shall come forth from it, and My people shall drink.” And Moses did so before the sons of Israel.
He named that place Testing and Reviling because the sons of Israel reviled and tested the Lord, saying, “Is the Lord among us or not?”
Amalek came and fought with Israel at Rephidim.

And Moses said to Joshua, “Choose for yourself able men, and go out and draw up for battle against Amalek tomorrow; and behold, I shall stand upon the summit of the hill, with the staff of God in my hand.”
Joshua did as Moses had told him and went out to take his stand against Amalek. Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
Whenever Moses raised his hands, Israel prevailed; whenever he lowered his hands, Amalek prevailed.
Moses’ hands were heavy. They took a stone, put it beneath him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur steadied his hands, one on each side, so that Moses’ hands remained supported until sunset.
Joshua routed Amalek and all his people with the slaughter of the sword.

And the Lord said to Moses, “Say to Aaron your brother, ‘Take your staff, and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, and over their canals, and over their marshes, and over all their standing water, and it shall become blood.’” And there was blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in wood and in stone.
Moses and Aaron did as the Lord commanded. He raised his staff and struck the river’s water before Pharaoh and his attendants, and all the water in the river turned to blood.
The fish in the river died, and the river stank. The Egyptians could not drink its water, and there was blood throughout the land of Egypt.
The king of the Egyptians spoke to the midwives of the Hebrews, one named Sepphora and the other Puah.
And he said, “When you attend the Hebrew women in childbirth, and they are about to give birth, if the child is male, kill him; but if the child is female, preserve her.”
But the midwives feared God. They did not do as the king of Egypt had commanded them, and they kept the boys alive.
And the king of Egypt called the midwives and said to them, “Why have you done this thing, and kept the male children alive?”
The midwives said to Pharaoh, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they give birth before the midwives come to them.” And they bore children.
God dealt well with the midwives, and the people multiplied and became very strong.
And because the midwives feared God, they made houses for themselves.
And Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, “Cast every male child born to the Hebrews into the river, but keep every female child alive.”
Now there was a man of the tribe of Levi, who took one of the daughters of Levi and had her as his wife.
She conceived and bore a male child. Seeing that he was beautiful, they hid him for three months.
When they could no longer hide him, his mother took a basket for him and coated it with bitumen-pitch. She put the child in it and placed it in the marsh beside the river.
His sister watched from a distance to learn what would happen to him.
Pharaoh’s daughter came down to bathe at the river while her attendants walked beside it. She saw the basket in the marsh, sent her attendant, and had it brought to her.
And she opened it, and saw a child weeping in the basket; and Pharaoh’s daughter had compassion on him, and said, “This is one of the Hebrew children.”
And his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Do you want me to call a nursing woman from among the Hebrews, that she may nurse the child for you?”
Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Go.” The young woman went and called the child’s mother.
And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Keep this child for me, and nurse him for me, and I will give you your wages.” And the woman took the child and nursed him.
When the child grew, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, saying, “I took him up out of the water.”
The Lord said to Moses, “I will bring one more plague upon Pharaoh and Egypt. Afterward he will let you go from here. When he lets you go, he will drive you out altogether, with everything.
Therefore speak secretly in the people’s hearing, and let each man ask his neighbour and each woman her neighbour for articles of silver and gold and for clothing.”
The Lord gave His people favour in the Egyptians’ sight, and they lent to them. The man Moses became very great in the sight of the Egyptians, Pharaoh, and all his attendants.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Say to Aaron your brother, ‘Stretch out the staff in your hand over the rivers, and over the canals, and over the marshes, and bring up the frogs.’”
Aaron stretched out his hand over Egypt’s waters and brought up the frogs. The frogs were brought up and covered the land of Egypt.
The Egyptian enchanters did the same by their sorceries and brought frogs up over the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said, “Pray to the Lord for me, and let Him remove the frogs from me and my people. I will let them go so that they may sacrifice to the Lord.”

And Moses said to Pharaoh, “Appoint a time for me to pray for you, and for your attendants, and for your people, to destroy the frogs from you and from your people and from your houses; only in the river shall they remain.”
And he said, “Tomorrow.” And he answered, “According to your word; that you may know that there is no other except the Lord.
And the frogs shall be removed from you, and from your houses, and from the farmsteads, and from your attendants, and from your people; only in the river shall they remain.”
Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh. Moses cried to the Lord concerning the appointed limit for the frogs, as Pharaoh had set it.
The Lord did as Moses said. The frogs died in the houses, farmsteads, and fields.
They gathered them in heaps upon heaps, and the land stank.
When Pharaoh saw that there was relief, his heart became heavy and he did not listen to them, as the Lord had said.

And the Lord said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Stretch out the staff in your hand, and strike the dust of the earth; and there shall be gnats upon men and upon four-footed animals, and throughout all the land of Egypt.’”
Aaron stretched out the staff in his hand and struck the earth’s dust, and gnats came upon people and four-footed animals. Gnats appeared in all the earth’s dust throughout the land of Egypt.
The enchanters tried by their sorceries to bring forth gnats, but they could not. The gnats were on people and four-footed animals.
The enchanters said to Pharaoh, “This is the finger of God.” But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, as the Lord had said.

And the Lord said to Moses, “Rise early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh; and behold, he shall go out to the water. And you shall say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord: Let My people go, that they may serve Me in the wilderness.

But if you will not let My people go, behold, I will send dog-flies upon you, and upon your attendants, and upon your people, and upon your houses; and the houses of the Egyptians shall be filled with dog-flies, and also the ground on which they stand.
And in that day I will marvellously distinguish the land of Goshen, in which My people dwell, so that no dog-flies shall be there; that you may know that I am the Lord, the Lord of all the earth.
And I will put a distinction between My people and your people; tomorrow this sign shall be upon the land.’”
Adoni-bezek fled, but they pursued him, seized him, and cut off the extremities of his hands and his feet.

Adoni-bezek said, “Seventy kings, with the extremities of their hands and feet cut off, used to gather what was beneath my table. As I have done, so God has repaid me.” They brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
In the beginning God made heaven and earth.
Now the earth was unseen and unformed, and darkness was over the deep; and the Spirit of God was moving over the water.
And God said, “Let there be light.” And there was light.
“Truly I know that it is so; for how can a mortal be righteous before the Lord?
For if he wishes to enter judgment with Him, He certainly will not listen to him, lest he answer back to one of His words out of a thousand.
For He is wise in understanding, mighty and great. Who grew hard against Him and endured?
He wears the mountains out, and they do not know; He overturns them in anger.
He shakes the world beneath heaven from its foundations, and its pillars sway.
He speaks to the sun and it does not rise, and He seals up the stars.
He alone stretched out heaven and walks on the sea as on ground.
He makes the Pleiades, the Evening Star, and Arcturus, and the storehouses of the south.
He does great and unsearchable things, glorious and extraordinary things beyond numbering.
If He passes over me, I will not see; if He passes by me, even then I do not perceive Him.
If He takes away, who will turn Him back? Who will say to Him, ‘What hast Thou done?’
If all the nations were counted like a drop from a bucket and like a scale’s slight tipping, they will also be counted like spittle.
Lebanon is not sufficient for burning, nor all the four-footed animals sufficient for a whole burnt offering,
and all the nations are as nothing and were counted as nothing.
Therefore you are without excuse, O man—whoever you are who judges. For when you judge another, you condemn yourself, because you who judge practice the same things.
And we know that God’s judgment against those who practice such things is according to truth.
But do you think, O man—you who judge those who practice such things and do them yourself—that you will escape God’s judgment?
Or do you despise the wealth of His kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that God’s kindness leads you to repentance?
Compassionate and merciful is the Lord, patient and abundant in mercy.
The Lord is kind to all, and His compassions are over all His works.
Let all Thy works give thanks unto Thee, Lord, and let Thy holy ones bless Thee.
A psalm of David, for the first day of the week. The earth and its fullness belong to the Lord, the inhabited world and all who dwell in it.
He founded it upon seas and prepared it upon rivers.

Do not say in your heart, when the Lord your God consumes these nations from before you: Because of my righteous deeds the Lord has brought me in to inherit this good land. Rather, because of the ungodliness of these nations the Lord shall destroy them from before you.

You do not enter to inherit their land for your righteousness, nor for the holiness of your heart; but because of the ungodliness of these nations the Lord shall destroy them from before you, and that He may establish His covenant which He sware unto your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
And when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not learn to do after the abominations of those nations.
There shall not be found among you one who purifies his son or his daughter by fire, or practises divination, or interprets spoken omens, or observes auguries, or works sorcery,
or chants spells, or is a medium, or observes portents, or inquires of the dead.
For everyone who does these things is an abomination unto the Lord your God; for because of these abominations the Lord shall destroy them from before you.
You shall be perfect before the Lord your God.
For these nations whose possession you inherit hearken unto omens and divinations; but the Lord your God has not granted you so to do.
They did not destroy the nations of which the Lord had spoken to them,
and mixed with the nations and learned their works.
They served their carved images, and it became a stumbling block to them.
They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons,
and shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters whom they sacrificed to Canaan’s carved images; the land was murdered with blood,
and was defiled by their works, and they prostituted themselves through their practices.
And if the Lord your God destroys from before you the nations whither you go to inherit their land, and you inherit their possession and dwell in their land,

take heed unto yourself, that you do not seek to follow them after they have been destroyed from before you. You shall not inquire after their gods, saying: How do these nations serve their gods? I also will do so.
You shall not do so unto the Lord your God; for the abominations which the Lord hated they did unto their gods, for they burn their sons and their daughters with fire unto their gods.
And I will send fear before you, and confound all the nations among whom you come; and I will make all your adversaries fugitives.
And I will send hornets before you, and they shall drive out the Amorites, and Hivites, and Canaanites, and Hittites from before you.
I will not drive them out in one year, lest the land become desolate, and the beasts of the land multiply against you;
little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you increase and inherit the land.
For the Lord shall judge His people, and be moved concerning His servants; for He saw them weakened, and failing under assault, and exhausted.
And the Lord said, Where are their gods, in whom they trusted,
whose sacrifices’ fat you ate, and whose drink offerings’ wine you drank? Let them arise and help you, and become your protectors.
See, see that I am, and there is no god beside Me. I will put to death, and make alive; I will smite, and I will heal; and there is none that shall deliver out of My hands.
Why did nations rage, and peoples meditate on empty things?
The kings of the earth stood ready, and the rulers gathered together, against the Lord and against His anointed. Diapsalma.
“Let us tear apart their bonds and cast their yoke away from us.”
The One dwelling in heaven will laugh at them, and the Lord will sneer at them.
Then He will speak to them in His anger and trouble them in His fury:
And Abraham drew near and said, “Wilt Thou destroy the righteous with the ungodly, and shall the righteous be as the ungodly?
If there are fifty righteous in the city, wilt Thou destroy them? Wilt Thou not spare the whole place for the sake of the fifty righteous, if they are there?
By no means shalt Thou do such a thing, to kill the righteous with the ungodly, so that the righteous shall be as the ungodly. By no means! Thou who judgest all the earth, wilt Thou not do justice?”
And the Lord said to Moses, “Rise early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh, and you shall say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Let My people go, that they may serve Me.
For at this time I will send all My blows upon your heart, and upon your attendants and your people, that you may know that there is none other like Me in all the earth.
For now I will stretch out My hand and strike you and your people with death, and you shall be blotted out from the earth.
And for this reason you were preserved, that I might show My strength in you, and that My name might be proclaimed throughout all the earth.
Do you still act against My people, refusing to let them go?
And Thou, Lord God, art compassionate and merciful, long-suffering, abundant in mercy, and true.
But love your enemies, do good, and lend, expecting nothing back. Your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, because He is kind to the ungrateful and evil.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Do not judge, and you will certainly not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will certainly not be condemned. Release, and you will be released.
Give, and it will be given to you. They will put into your lap a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, overflowing; for by the measure you measure, it will be measured back to you.”
And an angel of the Lord called to Abraham a second time out of the heaven,
saying, “By Myself I have sworn, says the Lord: because you have done this thing, and have not spared your beloved son for My sake,
surely I will bless you, and greatly multiply your seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand upon the shore of the sea; and your seed shall inherit the cities of their adversaries.
