And in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed, because you have listened to My voice.”
For God’s wrath is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of people who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,
because what is known of God is plain among them, for God made it plain to them.
For His invisible qualities, both His eternal power and divinity, have been clearly seen since the creation of the world, understood through the things made, so that they are without excuse,
because, although they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God or give thanks, but became futile in their thoughts, and their senseless heart was darkened.
Claiming to be wise, they became foolish,
and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible humanity, and of birds and four-footed animals and creeping things.
Therefore God handed them over, in the desires of their hearts, to impurity, so that their bodies would be dishonored among them,
who exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and revered and worshiped the creation instead of the Creator, who is blessed throughout the ages. Amen.
For this reason God handed them over to dishonorable passions; for their females exchanged natural relations for those contrary to nature,

and likewise the males, leaving natural relations with the female, burned in their desire for one another, males with males committing what is shameful and receiving in themselves the due penalty for their error.
And just as they did not see fit to retain God in their knowledge, God handed them over to an unfit mind, to do what is not fitting:
filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, evil; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, malice; whisperers,
slanderers, haters of God, insolent, proud, boastful, inventors of evils, disobedient to parents,
without understanding, faithless, without natural affection, merciless;
who, knowing God’s righteous decree, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, not only do them, but also approve those who practice them.
The God who made the world and everything in it, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in sanctuaries made by hands.
Nor is He served by human hands as though He needed anything, since He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything.
From one He made every nation of humanity to live upon the whole face of the earth, determining their appointed times and the boundaries of their dwelling,
so that they might seek God, if perhaps they might feel their way toward Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.
For in Him we live and move and exist, as even some of your own poets have said, ‘For we too are His offspring.’
Since we are God’s offspring, we ought not to think that the divine nature is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by human art and thought.
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, works of human hands.
They have a mouth and will not speak; they have eyes and will not see.
They have ears and will not hear; they have noses and will not smell.
They have hands and will not feel; feet, and will not walk; they will not sound with their throat.
May those who make them become like them, and all who have put their trust in them.
All who fashion and carve are futile, making what pleases them, things that will not help them. But they will be ashamed—
all who fashion a god and carve useless things,
and all from whom they came have dried up. Let the deaf from among humankind all assemble and stand together; let them be abashed and ashamed together.
For a craftsman sharpened iron, worked it with an adze, bored it with a drill, and worked it with his strong arm. He will hunger and grow weak and certainly not drink water. Having selected
wood, a craftsman set it by measure and arranged it with glue. He made it like a man’s form and human beauty, to set it in a house.
The wood he cut from the woodland was what the Lord planted and rain made grow,
so that it might serve people for burning. Taking some, he warmed himself; after burning it they baked loaves over the pieces. They worked the rest into gods and worship them.

Half of it they burned in fire, and after burning it they baked loaves over the pieces. Over it he roasted meat, ate, and was satisfied. Warmed, he said, ‘It is pleasant for me, for I am warm and have seen fire!’
He made the rest into a carved god and worships it and prays, saying, ‘Rescue me, for you are my god.’
They did not know enough to understand, because they were darkened from seeing with their eyes and comprehending with their heart.

He did not reckon it in his heart, consider it in his soul, or know by understanding that he burned half in fire, baked loaves over its coals, roasted meat and ate, and made its remainder an abomination; and they worship it.
Know that their heart is ashes, and they wander, and no one can rescue his soul. See—will you not say, ‘A lie is in my right hand’?
Hear the Lord’s word that He spoke concerning you, house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord: Do not learn according to the nations’ ways, and do not fear heaven’s signs, because they fear them before their faces.
For the nations’ customs are futile: it is wood cut from the woodland, a carpenter’s work and a cast object.
They are adorned with silver and gold; with hammers and nails they fastened them, and they will not move.
They must be lifted and carried, because they will not take a step. Do not fear them, because they certainly will not do evil, and no good is in them.
It is worked silver; they will not walk. Applied silver will come from Tarshish, gold from Mophaz, and the goldsmiths’ hand; all are artisans’ works. They will dress them in blue and purple.
This is what you will say to them: Gods who did not make heaven and earth, let them perish from the earth and from beneath this heaven.
The Lord who made the earth by His strength, who set the inhabited world upright by His wisdom, also stretched out heaven by His understanding,
and an abundance of water in heaven; and He brought clouds up from the earth’s extremity, made lightning for rain, and brought light out of His treasuries.
Every human became foolish, without knowledge; every goldsmith was put to shame at his carved things, because they cast false things; there is no spirit in them.
They are futile, mocked works; at the time of their visitation they will perish.
Jacob’s portion is not such as this, because the One who formed everything is himself his inheritance; Lord is His name.
Those going down into the sea in ships, doing work on many waters,
they saw the Lord’s works and His wonders in the depth.
He spoke, and a storm wind stood, and its waves were raised.
They rise as far as the heavens and descend as far as the deeps; their soul melted in evils.
They were troubled and shaken like a drunken man, and all their wisdom was swallowed up.
They cried to the Lord when they were afflicted, and He brought them out of their distresses,
and commanded the storm, and it settled into a breeze, and its waves fell silent.
They rejoiced because they became quiet, and He guided them to the harbor of their desire.
Thus says the Lord, who gives a way in the sea and a path in strong water,
who brought out chariots and a horse and a mighty host: But they fell asleep and will not rise; they were extinguished like an extinguished flax wick.
And it came to pass, when mankind began to increase upon the earth and daughters were born to them,
that the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and took wives for themselves from all whom they chose.
And the Lord God said, “My Spirit shall not abide in these men for ever, for they are flesh; and their days shall be a hundred and twenty years.”

Now giants were upon the earth in those days, and afterward also, whenever the sons of God went in to the daughters of men and they bore children to them. These were the giants of old, the men of renown.

You shall burn the graven images of their gods with fire. You shall not covet the silver or gold upon them, nor take it unto yourself, lest you stumble thereby; for it is an abomination unto the Lord your God.
And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, lest you become a thing under the ban, like unto it. You shall utterly reject it, and utterly abhor it, for it is a thing under the ban.

In the eighteenth year, King Nebuchadnezzar, who administered cities and countries and all who inhabited the earth from India to Ethiopia, made a golden image, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide. He set it up on the plain of the enclosure in the country of Babylonia.

Nebuchadnezzar, king of kings and lord of the whole inhabited world, sent to gather all the nations, tribes, and languages, satraps, generals, district governors, consuls, administrators, those holding authority in each country, and everyone throughout the inhabited world, to come to the dedication of the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Those previously listed stood opposite the image.
The herald proclaimed to the crowds, “You are commanded, nations and countries, peoples and languages:
when you hear the sound of trumpet, panpipe, kithara, sambuca, psaltery, symphonia, and every kind of musical instrument, fall down and bow to the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
They will throw into the blazing furnace anyone who does not fall down and bow.”

At that time, when all the nations heard the sound of the trumpet and every musical sound, all the nations, tribes, and languages fell down and bowed to the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up before him.
Hear the Lord’s word, sons of Israel, for the Lord has a case against the land’s inhabitants: there is no truth, no mercy and no recognition of God upon the land.
Cursing, falsehood, murder, theft and adultery have poured over the land, and they mix bloodshed with bloodshed.
He said to me, “This is the curse going out over the whole earth, because every thief will be punished by this with death, and every false swearer will be punished by this with death.

I will bring it out, says the Lord Almighty. It will enter the thief’s house and the house of whoever swears falsely by My name; it will lodge within his house and destroy it completely, its timbers and its stones.”
And you shall guard your souls diligently; for you saw no likeness in the day when the Lord spoke unto you in Horeb, on the mountain, out of the midst of the fire,
lest you act lawlessly and make for yourselves a graven likeness, any image, the likeness of male or female,
a likeness of any animal on the earth, a likeness of any winged bird flying beneath heaven,
the likeness of any creeping thing that creeps upon the earth, the likeness of any fish that is in the waters beneath the earth.

And lest you lift up your eyes unto heaven, and see the sun, and the moon, and the stars, and all the adornment of heaven, and be led astray to bow down unto them and serve them, which the Lord your God has allotted unto all the nations under heaven.
For Thou art not a God who desires lawlessness, nor will an evildoer sojourn with Thee.
The lawless will not remain before Thine eyes; Thou didst hate all who work lawlessness.
Thou wilt destroy all who speak falsehood; the Lord abhors a man of bloodshed and deceit.
I am the Lord God; this is My name. I will not give My glory to another or My praiseworthy deeds to carved images.
For from their small to their great, all have carried out lawless deeds; from priest to false prophet, all have done false things.
And they treated My people’s fracture with contempt, saying, ‘Peace, peace’; and where is peace?

They were put to shame because they failed, and even so they were not at all ashamed and did not recognize their dishonor. Therefore they will fall in their fall, and at the time of their visitation they will perish, said the Lord.
For which of these things should I be merciful to you? Your sons abandoned Me and swore by those who are not gods. And I fed them fully, and they committed adultery and lodged in prostitutes’ houses.
But who are you, O man, to answer back to God? Will what is formed say to the One who formed it, “Why didst Thou make me this way?”
Or does the potter not have authority over the clay, from the same lump to make one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?
But what if God, willing to demonstrate wrath and to make His power known, endured with much patience vessels of wrath fitted for destruction,
and did so to make known the wealth of His glory upon vessels of mercy, which He prepared beforehand for glory,
I saw all toil and all courage in work: it is a person’s rivalry with his companion. This too is futility and resolve of spirit.
Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this city, spend a year there, trade, and make a profit”—
you who do not know what tomorrow brings. What is your life? For you are a vapor, appearing for a little while and then disappearing.
Instead, you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we shall both live and do this or that.”
But now you boast in your pretensions. All such boasting is evil.
For those who share in murder store up evils for themselves, and the overthrow of lawless men is evil.
These are the ways of all who carry out lawless deeds, for through ungodliness they take away their own life.
And God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kind: four-footed animals, creeping things, and wild beasts of the earth according to their kind.” And it was so.

And God made the wild beasts of the earth according to their kind, and the cattle according to their kind, and all the creeping things of the earth according to their kinds. And God saw that they were good.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“I have heard the sons of Israel’s murmuring. Tell them: Toward evening you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall have your fill of bread. You shall know that I am the Lord your God.”
Evening came, and quail came up and covered the camp. In the morning, as the dew around the camp was subsiding,
there on the surface of the wilderness was something fine, like white coriander, like frost on the ground.
When the sons of Israel saw it, they said to one another, “What is this?” For they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, “This is the bread the Lord has given you to eat.
This is what the Lord commanded: Gather from it, each for those belonging to him, an omer per person according to your number. Each of you shall gather with your tent companions.”
The sons of Israel did so and gathered, some much and some little.
They measured it by the omer. The one with much had no excess, and the one with little had no lack. Each gathered for those belonging to his household.
Moses said to them, “Let no one leave any of it until morning.”
They did not listen to Moses. Some left part of it until morning, and it swarmed with worms and stank. Moses was embittered against them.
They gathered it morning by morning, each what he needed. When the sun grew hot, it melted.
On the sixth day they gathered twice what was needed, two omers per person. All the congregation’s leaders came in and reported it to Moses.

And Moses said to them, “This is the word which the Lord has spoken: Tomorrow is a Sabbath, a holy rest to the Lord. What you would bake, bake; and what you would boil, boil; and all that remains, lay up to keep until morning.”
They left some of it until morning, as Moses instructed them. It did not stink, and no worm was in it.
Moses said, “Eat today, for today is a Sabbath to the Lord. It will not be found in the field.
You shall gather for six days, but the seventh day is a Sabbath; there will be none on it.”
On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they found none.
And the Lord said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to listen to My commandments and My law?

Behold, the Lord has given you this day, the Sabbath. Therefore on the sixth day He gave you bread for two days. Each of you shall stay in your houses; no one shall go out from his place on the seventh day.”
The people kept Sabbath on the seventh day.
The sons of Israel called it Man. It was like coriander seed, white, and tasted like a cake with honey.
And they set out from Mount Hor by the road toward the Red Sea and went around the land of Edom. The people became fainthearted on the journey.
And the people spoke against God and against Moses: Why have you brought us out of Egypt to kill us in the wilderness? There is no bread or water, and our soul is disgusted with this empty bread.
And the Lord sent deadly serpents among the people. They bit the people, and many of the sons of Israel died.

And the people came unto Moses and said: We have sinned by speaking against the Lord and against you. Therefore pray unto the Lord, and let Him remove the serpents from us. Moses prayed unto the Lord for the people.
And the Lord said unto Moses: Make a serpent for yourself, and set it upon a standard; and it shall be, if a serpent bites a man, that everyone bitten, when he looks upon it, shall live.
And Moses made a bronze serpent and set it on a standard. Whenever a serpent bit a person, that person looked at the bronze serpent and lived.
But the Lord stood beside me and strengthened me, so that through me the proclamation might be fulfilled and all the nations might hear, and I was rescued from a lion’s mouth.
The Lord will rescue me from every evil work and save me into His heavenly kingdom. To Him be glory for the ages of ages. Amen.
And He commanded the clouds above and opened heaven’s doors,
and rained manna for them to eat, and gave them heaven’s bread.
A man ate angels’ bread; He sent them food supplies to fullness.
He moved the south wind from heaven, and brought the southwest wind by His power,
and rained flesh upon them like dust, and winged birds like the sands of seas,
and they fell within their camp, around their tents,
and they ate and were filled exceedingly, and He brought them their desire.
They were not deprived of their desire. While their food was still in their mouth,
then God’s wrath rose against them, and He killed among their fat ones, and entangled Israel’s chosen men.
and turned their rivers into blood, and their rain-waters, so that they might not drink.
He sent a dog-fly among them, and it devoured them, and a frog, and it destroyed them.
And He gave their fruit to mildew, and their labors to the locust.
He killed their vine with hail, and their sycamores with frost.
And He handed their cattle over to hail, and their possessions to fire.
He sent upon them the anger of His wrath, wrath, anger and affliction, a mission through evil angels.
He made a road for His wrath; He did not spare their souls from death, and confined their cattle to death,
and struck every firstborn in Egypt, the firstfruits of their labors in Ham’s tents.
And He led His people away like sheep, and brought them up like a flock in the wilderness,
and guided them in hope, and they did not grow cowardly; and the sea covered their enemies.
And He brought them into the boundary of His sanctuary, this mountain which His right hand acquired,
and expelled nations from before them, and assigned them by a cord of inheritance, and settled Israel’s tribes in their tents.
They cried to the Lord when they were afflicted, and He saved them from their distresses.
He sent His word and healed them and rescued them from their destructions.
Let them acknowledge to the Lord His mercies and His wonders to the sons of men,
and let them sacrifice a sacrifice of praise and proclaim His works in exultation.
The Lord puts to death and gives life; He brings down to Hades and brings up.

No human being has authority over the spirit to restrain the spirit, and there is no authority over the day of death. There is no discharge in war, and ungodliness will not rescue the one who possesses it.
Praise the Lord from the earth, dragons and all deeps,
fire, hail, snow, ice, storm wind—all fulfilling His word,
God, my God, toward Thee I rise at dawn; my soul thirsted for Thee. How greatly my flesh longs for Thee in a desert, trackless and waterless land!
And the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and let there be darkness upon the land of Egypt, darkness that may be felt.”
Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and there was darkness, gloom, and a tempest throughout the land of Egypt for three days.
No one saw his brother for three days, and no one rose from his bed for three days. But all the sons of Israel had light everywhere they lived.
Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said, “Go, serve the Lord your God. Only leave your sheep and your cattle behind. Let your household go with you.”
And Moses said, “You shall also give us whole burnt offerings and sacrifices, which we shall offer to the Lord our God.

Our livestock must also go with us. We will not leave a hoof behind, for we must take some of them to serve the Lord our God. We will not know with what we must serve the Lord our God until we arrive there.”
The Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was unwilling to let them go.
And Pharaoh said, “Depart from me! Take care not to see my face again; for on the day you appear before me, you shall die.”
And Moses said, “You have spoken; I will appear before your face no more.”
Moses and Aaron went before Pharaoh and his attendants and did as the Lord commanded. Aaron threw his staff before Pharaoh and his attendants, and it became a dragon.
Pharaoh summoned the wise men of Egypt and the sorcerers. The Egyptian enchanters did the same by their sorceries.
Each threw down his staff, and they became dragons. But Aaron’s staff swallowed their staffs.
Pharaoh’s heart grew strong, and he did not listen to them, as the Lord had said to them.

And upon those who remain of you I will bring cowardice into their heart in the land of their enemies; and the sound of a leaf borne along shall pursue them; and they shall flee as those fleeing from war, and fall when none pursues;
and brother shall disregard brother as in war, though no one runs after them. You shall not be able to withstand your enemies.
For whenever Gentiles who do not have law do by nature the things of the law, these, though not having law, are a law to themselves,
who show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience bearing witness with it, and their reasonings among themselves accusing or even defending,
on the day when God judges people’s secrets according to my gospel through Christ Jesus.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
“This month shall be the beginning of months for you; it shall be the first month of the year for you.
Speak to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, saying: On the tenth day of this month, each shall take a sheep for the ancestral households, one sheep for each household.

If those in the house are too few to be sufficient for a sheep, he shall join with his nearest neighbour. According to the number of persons, each person’s sufficient portion shall be reckoned for the sheep.
Your sheep shall be without blemish, a male a year old; you shall take it from the lambs and from the young goats.
And you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month; and the whole multitude of the congregation of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it toward evening.
They shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and the lintel of the houses in which they eat them.
They shall eat the meat that night, roasted over fire, and eat unleavened bread with bitter herbs.
You shall eat none of it raw, nor boiled in water, but roasted with fire, its head together with its feet and inward parts.
You shall leave none of it until morning, and you shall not break a bone of it. Whatever remains until morning you shall burn with fire.
And this is how you shall eat it: your loins girded, your sandals upon your feet, and your staffs in your hands; and you shall eat it in haste. It is a Passover to the Lord.
I will go through the land of Egypt that night and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human and animal. Against all the Egyptians’ gods I will execute vengeance. I am the Lord.
And the blood shall be a sign to you upon the houses in which you are; and I will see the blood, and shelter you; and no plague of destruction shall be among you when I strike the land of Egypt.
This day shall be a memorial for you. You shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord throughout all your generations; you shall celebrate it as a perpetual statute.
Moses called the whole council of elders of the sons of Israel and said to them, “Go and take a sheep for your families, and slaughter the Passover.
Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood beside the door, and touch the lintel and both doorposts with the blood beside the door. None of you shall go out of the door of his house until morning.

The Lord will pass through to strike the Egyptians. He will see the blood on the lintel and both doorposts, and the Lord will pass by the doorway. He will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses to strike.
And you shall keep this word as a statute for yourself and for your sons for ever.
And when you enter into the land which the Lord shall give to you, as He has spoken, you shall keep this service.
When your sons say to you, ‘What is this service?’

you shall say to them, ‘This Passover is a sacrifice to the Lord, because He sheltered the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when He struck the Egyptians and delivered our houses.’” The people bowed down and worshipped.
The sons of Israel went and did so. As the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.

At midnight the Lord struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on the throne to the firstborn of the captive woman in the pit, and the firstborn of every animal of the livestock.
Pharaoh rose during the night, with all his attendants and all the Egyptians. There was a great cry throughout the land of Egypt, for there was no house without someone dead.
And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron by night, and said to them, “Rise and depart from among my people, both you and the sons of Israel; go, serve the Lord your God, as you say.
Take your sheep and your cattle, and go. Bless me also.”
The Egyptians pressed the people hard to drive them quickly out of the land, for they said, “We are all dying!”
The people took their dough before it was leavened, with their kneaded batches wrapped in their garments on their shoulders.
The sons of Israel did as Moses had instructed them. They asked the Egyptians for articles of silver and gold and for clothing.
The Lord gave His people favour in the Egyptians’ sight, and they lent to them. Thus they plundered the Egyptians.
The sons of Israel departed from Rameses for Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, apart from the household company.
A great mixed multitude also went up with them, together with sheep and cattle and livestock in great abundance.

They baked the dough they had brought from Egypt into unleavened hearth-cakes, because it was not leavened. The Egyptians had driven them out, and they could not stay; nor had they prepared provisions for the journey.
The time the sons of Israel lived in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan was four hundred and thirty years.
After the four hundred and thirty years, all the Lord’s host went out from the land of Egypt.
It is a night vigil for the Lord, to bring them out of the land of Egypt. This same night is a vigil for the Lord for all the sons of Israel throughout their generations.
And the next day the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying: You have killed the Lord’s people!
And when the congregation banded together against Moses and Aaron, they rushed toward the Tent of Testimony. The cloud covered it, and the Lord’s glory appeared.
And Moses and Aaron came into the area before the Tent of Testimony.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Withdraw from the midst of this congregation, and I will consume them all at once. They fell on their faces.

And Moses said unto Aaron: Take the fire pan, put fire from the altar on it, and place incense on it. Carry it quickly into the camp and make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from before the Lord; it has begun to strike the people.
And Aaron took it just as Moses had told him and ran into the congregation. The outbreak had already begun among the people. He placed the incense and made atonement for the people,
and stood between the dead and the living, and the outbreak subsided.
And those who died in the outbreak numbered fourteen thousand seven hundred, apart from those who died because of Korah.
And Aaron returned unto Moses at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony, and the outbreak subsided.
You shall make an oracle-piece of judgments, embroidered work, according to the pattern of the shoulder-piece, of gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen.
It shall be square and doubled, a span long and a span wide.
You shall weave into it a fabric set with four rows of stones. The first row shall be a sardius, topaz, and emerald;
the second row a carbuncle, sapphire, and jasper;
the third row a ligure, agate, and amethyst;
the fourth row a chrysolite, beryl, and onyx. They shall be enclosed in gold and bound in gold according to their rows.
The stones shall bear the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
You shall make a full-length under-robe entirely blue.
And its neck opening shall be in the midst of it, with a border around the opening, the work of a weaver, its joining woven as one with it, so that it is not torn.

Around the under-robe’s lower hem you shall make little pomegranates like those of a flowering pomegranate tree, of blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen; likewise gold pomegranates, with bells between them all around.
Beside a gold pomegranate there shall be a bell and a floral ornament around the under-robe’s hem.
And Aaron’s sound shall be heard when he ministers, as he enters into the sanctuary before the Lord and as he goes out, so that he does not die.
You shall make a plate of pure gold and stamp on it like a seal: ‘The Lord’s consecrated thing.’
You shall fasten it to spun blue material so that it may rest on the headband, at the front of the headband.

It shall be on Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron shall remove the sins of the holy things the sons of Israel consecrate, of every holy gift. It shall be on Aaron’s forehead continually, acceptable for them before the Lord.

The king of the Egyptians was told that the people had fled. Pharaoh and his attendants had a change of heart toward the people and said, “What have we done, sending the sons of Israel away so that they no longer serve us?”
Pharaoh harnessed his chariots and took all his people with him.
He took six hundred chosen chariots, all the Egyptians’ horse force, and officers over all.
The Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt and of his attendants, and he pursued the sons of Israel. The sons of Israel were going out with a high hand.
The Egyptians pursued them and found them camped by the sea. All Pharaoh’s horse force and chariots, his horsemen, and his army were opposite the settlement, opposite Baal-zephon.
Pharaoh drew near. The sons of Israel looked up and saw the Egyptians camped behind them. They were very afraid, and the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord.

And they said to Moses, “Was it because there were no tombs in the land of Egypt that you brought us out to put us to death in the wilderness? What is this that you have done to us, bringing us out of Egypt?
Was this not the word which we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, ‘Leave us, that we may serve the Egyptians’? For it is better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in this wilderness.”

And Moses said to the people, “Take courage; stand, and behold the salvation from God, which He shall accomplish for us today. For as you have seen the Egyptians today, you shall see them no more for ever.
The Lord shall fight for you, and you shall keep silence.”
And the Lord said to Moses, “Why do you cry to Me? Speak to the sons of Israel, that they set forth.
And lift up with your staff, and stretch out your hand over the sea, and divide it; and let the sons of Israel enter into the midst of the sea upon dry ground.
Behold, I will harden the heart of Pharaoh and of all the Egyptians, and they will enter after them. I will be glorified through Pharaoh and all his army, his chariots, and his horses.
All the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord when I am glorified through Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horses.”
The one who brought the sheep’s shepherd up from earth remembered days of old. Where is the one who placed the holy spirit among them,
who led Moses by the right hand, the arm of His glory? He overpowered water before Him to make Himself an everlasting name.
He led them through the abyss like a horse through a wilderness, and they did not grow weary.
Like livestock through a plain, a spirit from the Lord came down and guided them. So Thou didst lead Thy people to make Thyself a glorious name.
The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned backward.
The mountains skipped like rams, and the hills like lambs of sheep.
What is it with you, sea, that you fled, and with you, Jordan, that you withdrew backward?
Mountains, that you skipped like rams, and hills, like lambs of sheep?
And the mixed company among them craved intensely, and the sons of Israel also sat down and wept, saying: Who will feed us meat?
We remember the fish we ate in Egypt for nothing, the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.
But now our life is parched; our eyes see nothing except the manna.
The manna is like coriander seed, and its appearance is like crystal.
And the people went about and gathered it, ground it in the mill, crushed it in the mortar, boiled it in the pot, and made cakes baked in ashes. Its pleasant taste was like a cake made with oil.
And when the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna fell upon it.

And a wind went out from the Lord and carried quail across from the sea. It cast them upon the camp, a day’s journey on this side and a day’s journey on that side, around the camp, about two cubits above the ground.

And the people rose all that day, all night, and all the following day and gathered quail. Whoever gathered least gathered ten kors, and they cooled them for themselves in cooling places around the camp.
And the two angels came to Sodom at evening; and Lot sat beside the gate of Sodom. And when Lot saw them, he rose up to meet them, and bowed his face to the earth,

and said, “Behold, my lords, turn aside into your servant’s house, and lodge there, and wash your feet; and you shall rise early and go on your way.” And they said, “No; but we will lodge in the square.”
And he urged them greatly; and they turned aside to him, and entered into his house. And he made them a feast with drink, and baked unleavened bread for them; and they ate.
Before they lay down, the men of the city, the Sodomites, surrounded the house, from young to old, all the people together.
And they called Lot out, and said to him, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, that we may lie with them.”
And Lot went out to them at the entrance, and shut the door behind him.
And he said to them, “By no means, brothers; do not act wickedly.

I have two daughters who have not known a man; I will bring them out to you, and do with them as you please. Only do nothing unjust to these men, for they have come under the shelter of my roof beams.”

And they said, “Stand back there. You came alone to live as a stranger; will you also pass judgment? So now we will afflict you more than them.” And they pressed hard upon the man, Lot, and drew near to break the door.
But the men stretched out their hands, and drew Lot to them into the house, and shut the door of the house.
And they struck the men who were at the door of the house with blindness, from small to great; and they became helpless in seeking the door.
And another king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
And he said to his nation, “Behold, the people of the sons of Israel are a great multitude, and are stronger than we are.
Come, therefore, let us deal craftily with them, lest they multiply; and when war befalls us, they also join our adversaries, wage war against us, and leave the land.”
He set overseers of labour over them to afflict them with their work. They built fortified cities for Pharaoh: Pithom, Rameses, and On, which is the City of the Sun.
But the more they humbled them, the more they multiplied and grew exceedingly, exceedingly strong; and the Egyptians loathed the sons of Israel.
The Egyptians oppressed the sons of Israel by force.
They made their lives painful with hard labour in clay and brickmaking, and with all the work in the plains, in every task in which they enslaved them by force.

And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Let them live in the land of Goshen; and if you know that there are able men among them, set them over my livestock.” And Jacob and his sons came into Egypt to Joseph; and Pharaoh king of Egypt heard. And Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, “Your father and your brothers have come to you.
“Behold, the land of Egypt is before you; settle your father and your brothers in the best of the land.”
But now thus says the Lord God who made you, Jacob, who formed you, Israel: “Do not fear, for I redeemed you. I called you by your name; you are Mine.
Even if you cross through water, I am with you, and rivers will not flood over you. Even if you pass through fire, you will certainly not be burned up; flame will not burn you up.
For I am the Lord your God, Israel’s Holy One, who saves you. I made Egypt your exchange, and Ethiopia and Soene on your behalf.
O depth of God’s wealth and wisdom and knowledge! How unsearchable His judgments and untraceable His ways!
“For who knew the Lord’s mind? Or who became His counselor?
Or who gave to Him first, and it will be repaid to him?”
Because from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory throughout the ages. Amen.
But if some true word had been among your words, none of these evils would have met you. Will not my ear receive extraordinary things from Him?
There were terrors and a nocturnal sound, fear falling upon people;
a shudder and trembling met me and shook my bones greatly.
A spirit came upon my face, and my hair and flesh shuddered.
I stood up and did not recognize it; I looked, and there was no form before my eyes, but I heard a breeze and a voice:
Repay no one evil for evil. Take thought for what is honorable before all people.
If possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with all people.
Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but make room for wrath; for it is written, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head.
Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.
In the last days the Lord’s mountain and God’s house will be clearly visible on the summits of the mountains and be raised above the hills; all the nations will come to it,

and many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. He will announce His way to us, and we will walk in it.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.
And about sunset a trance fell upon Abram; and behold, a great dark fear fell upon him.
And it was said to Abram, “Know for certain that your seed shall live as strangers in a land not their own; and they shall enslave them, and afflict them, and humble them for four hundred years.
But I will judge the nation they serve; and afterward they shall come out here with much baggage.
But you shall depart to your fathers in peace, buried at a good old age.
And in the fourth generation they shall return here; for the sins of the Amorites are not yet filled up.”
And as the sun was setting, a flame appeared; and behold, a smoking furnace, and torches of fire which passed between these divided pieces.
On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, “To your seed I will give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates:
And you shall say to Pharaoh, ‘Thus says the Lord: Israel is My firstborn son.
And I said to you, “Let My people go, that they may serve Me.” If therefore you will not let them go, behold, I will kill your firstborn son.’”

For the word of God is living and active and sharper than any two-edged sword, penetrating as far as the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
And no created thing is hidden before Him, but all things are naked and laid open to His eyes, to whom we must give account.
Moses entreated the Lord God and said, “Why, O Lord, art Thou angry with Thy people, whom Thou didst lead out of the land of Egypt with great strength and Thine uplifted arm?
Let not the Egyptians say, ‘He led them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and consume them from the earth.’ Cease from Thy fierce anger and be merciful concerning Thy people’s evil,

remembering Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Thy servants, to whom Thou didst swear by Thyself and speak, saying, ‘I will greatly multiply your seed as the stars of heaven in multitude’; and all this land which Thou didst say Thou wouldest give to their seed, they shall possess for ever.”
The Lord was appeased concerning the calamity He had said He would bring upon His people.

And God said, “Let the water beneath heaven be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear.” And it was so. And the water beneath heaven was gathered into its gathering places, and the dry land appeared.
And God called the dry land Earth, and the gathered waters He called Seas. And God saw that it was good.
The angel of God, who went before the camp of the sons of Israel, moved and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from before them and stood behind them.
It came between the Egyptians’ camp and Israel’s camp and stood there. There were darkness and gloom, and the night passed. They did not mingle with one another all night.
And Joseph said to all the Egyptians, “Behold, I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh. Take seed for yourselves, and sow the land.
“And of its produce you shall give a fifth part to Pharaoh; but the four parts shall be yours, for seed for the land, and for food for you and for all who are in your houses.”
And they said, “You have saved us; we have found grace before our lord, and we shall be Pharaoh’s slaves.”
What, then, shall we say? Should we remain in sin so that grace may increase?
May it never be! We who died to sin, how will we still live in it?
Or do you not know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?
Therefore we were buried with Him through baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the Father’s glory, so we also might walk in newness of life.
Jesus spoke these things, and, lifting His eyes to heaven, said, “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Thy Son, so that the Son may glorify Thee,
just as Thou gavest Him authority over all flesh, so that He may give eternal life to them—to all that Thou hast given Him.
And this is eternal life: that they know Thee, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom Thou didst send.
